items.statement: EBITDA margins consistent in 24%-25% range over last five years
items.quote: if you look at our track record we have grown consistently in double-digits over the last five years and our margins have also been consistent in the 24%, 25% EBITDA range.

items.statement: Payer margin compression (MLRs rising to high 80s/90%+) driving cost takeout demand; outsourcing penetration only in low 20s leaving 70%+ work in-house
items.quote: The MLRs have gone up from the low 80s to high 80s and in some cases even 90 plus. What that basically tells you is payers are increasingly spending over 90% of their premiums in just paying claims.

items.statement: Shift to outcome-based managed services and Synchrony platform deals; one managed services deal expanded scope from $6M to $20M annual revenue (3.5x) over 5 years
items.value: 3.5x revenue growth on managed services deal
items.quote: think from our perspective 6 million possibly declining now becomes instead of 30 million over five year or less. Now is a 100 million for us. So that's a 3.5x growth for us in terms of revenue.

items.statement: Willing to invest upfront in client transformations and straight-line savings over contract period; open to multiple pricing constructs including base fee + ARR linked to membership
items.quote: We will make the investments on their behalf and we will straight line the savings for them over a period of time.

items.statement: Internal AI initiatives to reimagine hiring, training, operations; expected big impact on cost of doing business in next 12-18 months
items.quote: we believe in the next 12 to 18 months that's going to have a big impact on the cost of doing business for us

items.statement: Regulatory constraints (HIPAA, clinical decision autonomy limits), fragmented data/legacy systems, and stakeholder complexity limit fully autonomous AI deployment; human-in-loop required
items.quote: when we try and implement AI and Agentic AI in healthcare. You got to be careful that what you do is auditable, what you do is explainable and what you do is compliant.

items.statement: 21 mid-market payer plans (<1M members) targeted for Synchrony Utilization Management with partners; pipeline building across managed services, Synchrony, MLR reduction
items.quote: right now we are I think Krithika will probably have the right numbers 21 identified plans where our Synchrony Utilisation Management with the partners is being targeted for.

items.statement: AI viewed as force multiplier not disruptor; Gen AI enabling expansion into onshore/restricted work previously unaddressable; enterprise transformation framework created for clients
items.quote: We are looking at AI as a force multiplier. We are not looking at AI as a disruptor.

items.statement: Enterprise transformation pipeline of projects worth around $45 million created for a client, with Sagility as convener.
items.quote: we created an overall enterprise pipeline of projects worth close to around 45 million.

items.statement: Saved close to $15 million of late claim payment interest for a client in 2025 via Appeals Command Centre.
items.quote: For that particular use case for 2025, we saved close to around $15 million of late claim payment interest.

items.statement: Process reengineering project alone saved close to $4.5 million, part of the $11.4 million admin cost reduction.
items.quote: that project alone saved close to around $4.5 million which is part of this $11.4 million.

items.statement: Single payer-provider transaction costs around $8 to $10 on average across channels.
items.quote: a single transaction from a payer and a provider across different channels on an average cost around $8 to $10.

items.statement: Alternate digital channels with agentic enablement can reduce transaction cost by close to 60-70%.
items.quote: you can reduce the cost by say close to 60%, 70%.

items.statement: Managed services point solutions deliver 15-20% incremental savings; Synchrony delivers higher savings.
items.quote: the ability for you to impact in terms of the value is still dollars in terms of 15%, 20% incremental savings because you are still working on the client’s platform.

items.statement: Committed to around $5 million saving over $20 million contract on managed services side.
items.quote: we have committed to a saving of around 5 million over 20 million that's typically a percentage that we look at

items.statement: Synchrony Medicare Advantage solution productised and ready for next open enrolment season in 2026.
items.quote: Today this is something that we have launched as a productised offering and we are ready for next open enrolment which is the next season coming up in 2026.

items.statement: UM programs typically reduce 5-15% of medical spend; industry opportunity is $200-300 billion.
items.quote: UM typically can reduce anywhere between 5% to 15% of medical spend.

items.statement: Quality of care programs deliver 30% lower admission rates and 3x to 5x ROI.
items.quote: 30% lowered admission rates and more importantly programs like this really have 3x to 5x ROI

items.statement: Client engagement resulted in about $24 million savings by enhancing UM and bundling care management.
items.quote: resulting in about a $24 million savings for not spending too much more on the UM operation.

items.statement: Gen AI costs can run up if applied to every problem on large language models; need to balance cost, accuracy, latency.
items.quote: if you were to attempt to apply Gen AI for every last problem and you were to build it on the backs of these foundational models, especially the large language models, the cost can run up.

items.statement: Heavily invested in Gen AI over last 24 months including an acquisition in the generative AI space.
items.quote: Over the last 24 months, we even made an acquisition, which you all probably know about in the generative AI space, brought some capabilities in

items.statement: Management expects to continue growing at historical rates of low double-digits to mid-teens for the near term.
items.quote: we will continue to grow at historical rates in the, like I said, low double -digits to mid -teens kind of a number

items.statement: Management is comfortable with current margin levels and aims to retain them while passing AI-driven efficiencies to clients to fuel growth.
items.quote: broadly, we are happy with the margins where they are, so we'll try our best to retain these margins, while utilising the benefits that we generate to help us continue to grow

items.statement: No specific capex guidance given; focus is on AI-driven revenue per FTE improvement rather than headcount reduction.
items.quote: if you look at like-to-like, if I look at the revenue per FTE per employee in India today versus what it's likely to be two years or three years down the road, it's likely to show a significant movement upwards

items.statement: Payer revenue split: ~1/3 claims, ~1/3 clinical & payment integrity, ~1/3 member & provider lifecycle.
items.quote: One-third of our payer revenues are claims revenues, one -third of our payer revenues are your clinical and payment integrity and the other one -third is a member and provider life cycle

items.statement: Client adoption of AI is gated by regulatory complexity, data readiness, governance committees, and legacy platform replacement cycles.
items.quote: a lot of times our use cases, while we have the capability to deploy some use cases, we are waiting for clients to give us permission to do that

items.statement: Partnership ecosystem (advisors, tech partners) is accelerating pipeline and shortening sales cycles to ~6 months.
items.quote: If a third-party is involved, it's much shorter. Yes, closer to the six, right

items.statement: Pricing shifting from FTE/hourly to outcome-based models (managed services, MLR, transaction rates) to share AI-driven efficiencies.
items.quote: we started doing 25, 26 claims. Then we said that look, how are we doing this? Why don't we convert into transaction rates so that we share the benefits together?

items.statement: Internal engineering productivity gains from Gen AI tools are promising; first measurements underway after ~1 year of adoption.
items.quote: we're coming up to a point where we're having our first measurement of the impact on that productivity gains. And the data so far is quite promising

items.statement: EPL maintains double-digit revenue growth guidance; combined entity targets emerging market growth.
items.quote: Our guidance on EPL remains unchanged of double-digit revenue growth in the future.

items.statement: Merger expected to complete in approximately 12 months, subject to regulatory approvals.
items.quote: Completion of merger process is subject to regulatory approvals and is expected to take approximately 12 months.

items.statement: Synergies of $35-50 million annually identified across footprint, product, and costs.
items.quote: We've identified synergies of ~$35 million to $50 million across geographical footprint, product capabilities and costs, which will drive an EBITDA upside over the next few years.

items.statement: Post-merger debt-to-EBITDA to fall to 0.25 from 0.65, enhancing balance sheet.
items.quote: As a result of this merger, our debt-to-EBITDA ratio will come down to 0.25, and therefore we will have significant investment ability.

items.statement: Combined entity to have revenue of INR8,300 crores and EBITDA of ~INR1,750 crores.
items.value: INR8,300 crores revenue, INR1,750 crores EBITDA
items.quote: Together, we are creating a diversified multiformat packaging platform that doubles our combined revenue to INR8,300 crores and EBITDA to approximately INR1,750 crores.

items.statement: Indovida's CY25 performance impacted by high base and weather; long-term volume CAGR 8%.
items.quote: In the long term, and this is data which you can access, the volume CAGR of Indovida is 8%, including both organic and inorganic growth, and that's really positive in this business.

items.statement: Cost inflation passed through to customers; no margin risk expected.
items.quote: There is no risk on the margin.

items.statement: Indovida plans to enter Morocco and Algeria; recently entered Tanzania.
items.quote: They recently entered Tanzania and now they are planning to enter Morocco and Algeria as well.

items.statement: Post-merger, IVL to hold 51.8% and Blackstone 16.6%; both remain promoters.
items.quote: Post-merger, IVL will hold 51.8% of MergeCo and will be promoter of EPL.

items.statement: Combined entity to generate ~$200 million EBITDA with 60-65% cash conversion.
items.quote: So the combined business, Mayank, would generate about $200 million of EBITDA. Both companies, EPL as well as Indovida, have a very healthy cash to EBITDA conversion ratio with about 60% to 65% of EBITDA getting converted into cash.

items.statement: Indovida's working capital is 50 days; 90% of EBITDA is operating cash flow.
items.quote: So, the working capital for Indovida business is 50 days and the operating cash flow, so the working capital investments are limited in line with the revenue investments, about 90% of EBITDA is the operating cash flow.

items.statement: Majority of minority shareholder approval required for the merger.
items.quote: Yes, majority of minority. I mean we will need to get that approval.

items.statement: EPL valued at INR339 per share, 70% premium; Indovida at 8.1x EBITDA.
items.quote: EPL was valued at INR339 per share, ~70% premium to Friday's closing price.

items.statement: Combined entity to have ~INR51 crores shares post-merger.
items.quote: As part of the transactions, we will issue INR 18.5 crores additional shares and hence the total number of shares would be around INR51 crores.

items.statement: Positive on FY27 growth, expects stronger first half; no specific number given.
items.quote: We are also expecting a stronger 1H. Our planning assumption is along those lines only.

items.statement: Most known client-specific headwinds are behind; no major new headwinds expected.
items.quote: By and large, most of the headwinds we know probably are behind us, excepting few that may come up or that we have already accounted for.

items.statement: Wage increments to impact margins 150-200 bps, similar to past cycles.
items.quote: On the wage increments, you should expect a similar impact on what we have seen in the past annual increment cycle, which had been in the range of 150 to 200 basis points.

items.statement: Aims to move toward 26% margin on a longer-term basis.
items.quote: Overall, we'd want to balance it and keep margins within a tighter reach. We'd like to move towards 26%, but on a longer-term basis.

items.statement: SG&A to stay elevated in absolute and percentage terms due to Build-Partner-Acquire investments.
items.quote: Some part of it will see an elevated increase, both in the absolute amount as well as in percentage of revenue.

items.statement: Q4 TCV of $12 billion including three mega deals.
items.quote: Our order book performance was also very strong in Q4, with $12 billion in TCV including three mega deal wins from Marks and Spencer, a leading telecom operator in the UK, and a leading American healthcare & pharmacy retailer.

items.statement: Deal mix roughly 50-55% renewals, 40-45% new programs.
items.quote: I think this quarter maybe about 50% to 55% could be on renewals, around 40% to 45% would be on new programs.

items.statement: Annualized AI services revenue crossed $2.3 billion.
items.quote: In Q4, our annualized AI revenues surpassed $2.3 billion, driven by the accelerated deployment of AI solutions across industries.

items.statement: AI expected net accretive; aims to arrest degrowth while AI revenue rises.
items.quote: But, of course, over a period of time, AI revenue or AI related revenue, because it will become very difficult to classify after some time on what is AI, what is AI adjacent revenue, but ensure that they all grow, we will expect them to grow much faster.

items.statement: HyperVault building 1 GW capacity; OpenAI partnership 100 MW with option to scale to 1 GW.
items.quote: We have partnered with Open AI to build 100 MW capacity, with an option to scale to 1 GW.

items.statement: HyperVault demand converging around 100-200 MW anchor AI workloads per customer.
items.quote: We see the demand converging around large, anchor AI workloads in the 100–200 MW range per customer.

items.statement: Geopolitical impact so far limited to Middle East and travel & transportation.
items.quote: But at this time, I think the impact will be limited to our travel and transportation and probably the work we do in Middle East.

items.statement: Does not lose deals on pricing; strong margins give flexibility to compete.
items.quote: We don't lose deals on pricing. We work with our customers, we ensure that we give the best solution, and we've been able to win deals.

items.statement: Restructuring program completed; no one-offs in Q4.
items.quote: The restructuring program that we started, we have completed that program. The program towards restructuring has been completed.

items.statement: FY27 revenue guidance of INR 1,415 crores.
items.quote: We have given FY '27 revenue guidance of INR 1,415 crores and PAT guidance of INR 460 crores, again, going with the principles which Rakesh sir Rawal and Rathi ji has always taught and every elder in the company has taught us that under commit, over deliver.

items.statement: FY27 PAT guidance of INR 460 crores.
items.quote: Under the same principle, we are guiding you INR 1,415 crores and INR 460 crores for PAT and INR 1,20,000 crores of AUM for the year ending FY '27 is our guidance.

items.statement: Crossed INR 1 lakh crores AUM post recent equity market movement.
items.quote: As of yesterday's date, we have crossed INR1 lakh crores of AUM post the recent positive movement in the equity markets.

items.statement: Board approved 1:1 bonus issue and final dividend of INR 7 per share.
items.quote: As a part of our policy to reward shareholders, the Board has approved the bonus issuance of 1:1 and has declared a final dividend of INR 7 per equity share, both subject to shareholders' approval.

items.statement: FY26 PAT ended at INR 386 crores versus INR 375 crores guided.
items.value: INR 386 crores vs INR 375 crores guided
items.quote: Excluding the impact of fair value gains on the ESOP expense and the related tax effects for FY '26, our total revenue grew by 22%, and we ended the year at INR 1,198 crores with a PAT growth of 28% for the year, ending at INR 386 crores against the INR 375 crores guided.

items.statement: FY26 net inflows grew 7% to INR 13,457 crores.
items.quote: Then coming to the net flow of last year grew by 7% only, INR 13,457 crores is what we collected new, thanks to our clients who have been very generous to give us more money during bad times.

items.statement: Added 1,600 net new client families; total 13,395 families.
items.quote: In our flagship Wealth Management business in the last 12 months, we have added 1,600 new client families on a net basis, bringing our total number to 13,395 individual families.

items.statement: FY26 client attrition by AUM was 0.54%.
items.quote: Client attrition rate in terms of AUM lost for FY '26 is 0.54% for the full year.

items.statement: Digital wealth AUM grew 22% YoY to INR 2,218 crores; clients up 17% to 7,106.
items.quote: Digital wealth business, which is a B2B2C business, registered an AUM growth of 22% year-on-year to INR 2,218 crores and the number of clients increased by 17% to 7,106.

items.statement: OFA SaaS platform has 6,906 subscribers and INR 1.47 lakh crores platform assets.
items.quote: The OFA business, Omni Financial Advisors business, which is a SaaS platform, has 6,906 subscribers with a platform assets of INR1.47 lakh crores for the year ended 31 st March 2026.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 PAT margin flat at 30.5% YoY.
items.quote: Profit after tax margin remained flat at 30.5% for Q4 FY '26, which was at the same level in Q4 FY '25 too.

items.statement: FY26 PAT margin improved to 32.2% from 30.7% in FY25.
items.quote: Profit after tax margin improved from 30.7% in FY '25 to 32.2% for FY '26.

items.statement: FY26 ROE annualized at 46.74%.
items.quote: Return on equity on an annualized basis stood at best in industry at 46.74% for FY '26.

items.statement: Management expects to hold margins steady for the next 5 years with a very full order book through 2031.
items.quote: We believe we will hold margins very steady for the next 5 years or so. Every major project that's offered from OEMs till their launch in 2031, we will fund. So our order book is very, very full.

items.statement: Capex intensity for the target business is guided between 1.5% and 3.5% of total net sales annually.
items.quote: let's say between 1.5% and 3.5% investment of the total net sales is what you also see in the business case. So very, very intelligent way of investments.

items.statement: Target acquisition is margin accretive from day one and the trend is expected to continue for many years.
items.quote: The company is also very good with margins right now. So on day one, it's margin accretive which is a very positive thing, very rarely happens in a transaction like this. And this trend continues for us for many years.

items.statement: Order book is very full with all major OEM projects funded through 2031 launches; no significant orders lost.
items.quote: Every major project that's offered from OEMs till their launch in 2031, we will fund. So our order book is very, very full. Maybe not lost any order maybe not so far.

items.statement: No capacity will be added for unlegislated two-wheeler ABS segment until legislation or firm OEM orders provide certainty.
items.quote: we plan capacity based on either a upcoming legislation or based on an OEM part. So we will not simply add lines and just wait and depreciate those margins, so we are not doing that.

items.statement: Pro forma EPS accretion of approximately 5% expected based on FY25 numbers
items.quote: RBIC acquisition immediately strengthens our financial profile with an expected pro forma EPS accretion of approximately 5% based on FY25 numbers.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue to increase 22% to INR22,000 crores on pro forma basis for FY25
items.quote: Bosch Limited's consolidated revenue from operations will increase by 22% from INR18,000 crores to INR22,000 crores on a pro forma basis for FY25.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin to improve to 13.9% on pro forma basis from 12.8%
items.quote: The FY25 EBITDA margins will improve from 12.8% to 13.9% on a pro forma basis led by higher margins of RBIC.

items.statement: Order book very full with strong project pipeline for next 4-5 years
items.quote: Yes, see the current order book is very full. It's the market leader, very good market share across all categories and very good project pipeline for the next four to five years.

items.quote: The growth for this portfolio is driven by structural tailwinds. First, a strong regulatory push. We are seeing a clear roadmap for enhanced vehicle safety in India with mandates for airbags, ABS, ESP, and adoption of Bharat New Car Assessment Program.

items.statement: Revenue mix roughly one-third 2-wheeler, two-thirds 4-wheeler (PV+CV)
items.quote: We can say roughly one-third is 2-wheeler and the other one is 4-wheeler. So this is more or less the share in the revenues.

items.quote: The purchase consideration for the transaction is INR9,068.70 crores. RBIC's valuation is at an implied 10.6x EV over FY25 EBITDA. We intend to fund the transaction through existing funds and internal accruals.

items.statement: No synergies counted in business case; post-merger integration may yield future synergies
items.quote: Nevertheless, after the approval of the transaction in the post-merger integration period, we will have a look if we bring these two companies as a mother company Bosch Limited and a subsidiary for the chassis systems under one roof let's say, are there further synergies.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 IT Services revenue guidance of -2% to 0% sequential growth in constant currency
items.quote: In Q1, we are guiding for a sequential growth of minus 2% to 0% in constant currency terms.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 operating margin at 17.3%, down 30 bps sequentially; full year FY26 margin at 17.2%, up 15 bps YoY
items.quote: Our operating margin came in at 17.3%, a contraction of 30 basis points sequentially.

items.statement: Management aims to maintain margins in narrow band medium-term despite wage hikes, large deal ramp-ups, and AI investments
items.quote: our endeavour would be to maintain these margins in a narrow band in the medium term

items.statement: Board approved buyback of INR 15,000 crores at INR 250 per share, largest ever, expected to complete in Q1 FY27
items.quote: the Board of Directors have announced and approved a buyback of INR15,000 crores at a price of INR250 per share

items.statement: Strong pipeline across markets and sectors; BFSI showing good traction in Europe and APMEA, US BFSI spending on AI, data, cloud continues

items.quote: we have launched a dedicated AI-native business and platforms unit to expand beyond a services-only model to a services-as-a-software approach

items.statement: Americas 2 BFSI weakness from client-specific issues and delayed large deal ramp-ups; one client issue ends in Q1, ramp-up delays expected to resolve
items.quote: This has been a combination of both client-specific issue and delayed ramp-up that that you're talking about

items.quote: We maintained the margins within a narrow band even after absorbing two incremental months of DTS HARMAN. And we also rolled out salary increases effective first March

items.statement: FY27 capex guided at INR900 crores, FY28 at INR960 crores, largely for Vadraj refurbishment
items.quote: '27 and '28 will be INR900 crores for '27 and INR960 crores for '28. That's all largely coming out of Vadraj refurbishment, INR627 crores and INR728 crores.

items.statement: Vadraj Cement project on schedule; clinker and grinding units to commission in phases between Q3 FY27 and Q1 FY28
items.quote: The clinker unit and grinding units are planned to be commissioned in phases between Q3 FY '27 and Q1 FY '28.

items.quote: Already, we are looking at close to about INR100 per ton increase due to packing bags cost increase and granular cost increase and conversion cost increase, which has happened.

items.quote: In our core states of Bihar, Bengal, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, there is good demand. And in terms of the first 13, 14 days of the month, our pro rata is as per our plan.

items.statement: FY26 operating margin improved to 37.6 bps from 35.9 bps in FY25

There is no much difference that we see between March and April, right?

items.statement: Final dividend of INR 12.4 per share declared for FY26, subject to shareholder approval

items.quote: Our solvency ratio stood at 177%. While we await clarity on the transition timeline to the risk-based solvency framework

items.statement: Vibha Padalkar CEO tenure ends September 2026; IRDA 15-year rule applies from MD/CEO appointment date (8 years completed)
items.quote: My tenure, this current tenure ends in September of this year, and the Board will take a suitable call closer to that date

items.statement: Management expects to neutralize GST impact in H1 FY27 and target FY25 margin levels of 25%+, but prioritizes growth over margin expansion
items.quote: before GST, or rather I think end of quarter three we did mention that we'd like to get back to the levels of FY25 in the 25-plus percent range. Can we get to it? We possibly can, but like I mentioned earlier on the call, that's not something we're going to prioritize.

items.statement: No specific APE growth guidance for FY27 due to volatility; aim to grow slightly faster than sector while focusing on protection headwinds and Tier 2/3 traction
items.quote: I think we will just take it a month at a time in terms of planning. It is really volatile. What we will attempt to do is grow slightly faster than the sector and while doing that focus on some of the headwinds that we have on protection.

items.statement: AGNI variable annuity launched in Q4 FY26 to become full-stream product in FY27; non-par savings enhancements planned for Click 2 Achieve series
items.quote: AGNI was basically the first variable annuity product that was introduced and it's absolutely contributed to our share of annuity mix increasing meaningfully in this period. And it was launched towards in the last quarter, so we expect that to become a full-stream product going into FY27 and beyond.

items.statement: AGNI variable annuity margins higher than company-level margins
items.quote: It will be higher than company-level margins.

items.statement: Non-par take-up expected to be higher in FY27 vs FY26 despite current equity flows; product suite ready for favorable rate environment
items.quote: we absolutely believe this year I think the non-par take-up should be higher than what it was last year. It's a bit puzzling why it hasn't happened already.

items.statement: Retail protection demand strong post-GST: 80% new-to-HDFC Life customers, average ticket size maintained, far from saturation
items.quote: post-GST about 80% of the protection business is new to HDFC Life customers that we saw. And as Vibha mentioned in her opening comments, we're basically seeing fair bit of demand across different customer segments.

items.statement: HDFC Bank counter share: mid-60s% in FY25, early-60s% in FY26; medium-term target two-thirds; HDFC Bank contributes ~40% of individual NBP
items.quote: we were in mid-60s the year before, and this year we would have closed at early 60s.

items.statement: Branch expansion: 200+ branches opened in past 24-36 months; 13% of agency business from new branches; Tier 2/3 growing faster than Tier 1
items.quote: we've been opening branches, you know over 200-plus branches over the past 24 to 36 months, and happy to share that in our agency channel, 13% of the business now comes from the branches that we opened in that time frame.

items.statement: Capital raise: INR 1,000 cr equity + INR 500 cr sub-debt capacity = 1,300-1,400 bps solvency boost; dividend kept flat at INR 450 cr
items.quote: We could raise on the back of INR 1,000 crores of equity, INR 500 crores sub-debt, which will give us an additional 4% as and when we believe it would be required or we want to just exercise that option.

items.statement: Persistency sensitivity increased due to higher ULIP mix and surrender value regulation changes impacting non-linked margins
items.quote: One is the proportion of ULIP has gone up compared to last year. Hence, higher sensitivity. And also because of the changes in surrender value regulations, even in the non-linked products, the persistency will have an impact on the EV or the margin.

items.statement: MFI credit life growth: 40%+ in Q4 FY26 on subdued base; ~13% for full FY26
items.quote: Quarter four MFI growth was there because there was also a subdued base last year, growth was in excess of 40% in Q4, while on an overall year basis, I think we saw business growth of about 13-odd percent.

items.statement: Non-par demand not elastic to IRR within 15-20% band; pricing matters only at outlier levels; brand and distribution drive choice
items.quote: in protection 15%-20% up and down, it is not elastic, it is driven by multiple things including brand preference and as long as we're in the zone we are okay.

items.statement: GST impact on existing book treated as one-time variance; new business impact baked into FY27 VNB; yield curve changes captured dynamically in product profile not as separate assumption change
items.quote: the GST impact is the impact on the existing business because there is no input tax credit on the renewal commission and the maintenance expenses. So that is a one-time impact and it is external environmental impact, that is why it is shown as another operating change or variance.

items.statement: Jio Credit quarterly disbursements crossed Rs 10,600 crore in Q4 FY26, up 49% YoY
items.quote: The disbursements in Q4 FY26 of over Rs. 10,600 crore—representing a 49% YoY increase—were completely organic and stand as a testament to the connection we have been able to build with our customers.

items.statement: Jio Credit capital adequacy ratio at 25.91% as of March 31, 2026
items.quote: while the Debt-to-Equity ratio remained comfortable at a little over 3 times, even as we continue to maintain a very robust capital adequacy ratio of 25.91%.

items.statement: Jio Payments Bank deposit base grew 84% YoY to Rs 544 crore
items.quote: Correspondingly, our deposit base grew to Rs. 544 crore, up 84% from Rs. 294 crore in the previous year.

items.statement: Jio Payment Solutions TPV crossed Rs 52,200 crore in FY26, up 2.5x YoY
items.quote: At Jio Payment Solutions, Total Transaction Processing Volume, or TPV, crossed the Rs. 50,000 crore-mark in FY26, and stood at over Rs. 52,200 crore, a 4.1x growth over FY24, and 2.5 times the TPV processed in FY25.

items.statement: Jio Payment Solutions Net Processing Margin improved to 12 bps in Q4 FY26 from 6 bps YoY
items.quote: Our Net Processing Margin improved to 12 basis points in Q4 FY26, up from 6 basis points a year ago and 10 basis points in the preceding quarter.

items.statement: JioBlackRock AMC AUM reached over Rs 15,200 crore within 9 months of launch
items.quote: JioBlackRock Asset Management's AUM stood at over Rs. 15,200 crore at the end of FY26, within just 9 months of launch.

items.statement: Jio Insurance Broking facilitated Rs 273 crore premium in Q4 FY26, up 15% YoY
items.quote: Our insurance broking entity, Jio Insurance Broking, facilitated a premium of Rs. 273 crore in Q4 FY26, a 15% increase year-on-year.

items.statement: Consolidated Total Income grew 78% YoY to Rs 3,274 crore in FY26
items.quote: Our Consolidated Total Income, excluding dividends, grew to Rs. 3,274 crore in FY26, a 78% increase over FY25.

items.statement: Treasury income impacted by steep increase in yields in late March 2026 due to geopolitical tensions
items.quote: Third, we witnessed a steep increase in treasury yields in late March 2026 driven by geopolitical tensions. This volatility impacted our treasury income, especially considering our high capital base at this juncture of our evolution.

items.statement: Company refrains from giving specific quantitative guidance on future performance
items.quote: As a policy, company refrains from giving specific quantitative guidance on its future performance.

items.statement: Crisil expects India GDP growth at 7.1% base case for this fiscal, downside risk to 6.8% if West Asia conflict prolongs through April
items.quote: Crisil expects India's GDP, Gross Domestic Product to grow at 7.1% in the base case for this fiscal, compared with 7.6% in the last fiscal.

items.statement: Global growth forecast to moderate to 3.2% in 2026, US economy expected to grow 2.2% in 2026
items.quote: We forecast global growth to moderate to 3.2% in 2026. Against this backdrop, the US economy is expected to remain resilient, growing to 2.2% in 2026.

items.statement: Bank credit growth expected around 13% in fiscal 2027 driven by MSME and retail segments
items.quote: We expect the bank credit to grow at around 13% in fiscal 2027, driven by healthy growth in MSME and retail segment.

items.statement: Corporate profitability estimated flat in fiscal 2026 and decline around 100 basis points in FY2027 due to West Asia crisis disruptions
items.quote: We estimate the corporate profitability to remain almost flat in fiscal 2026 and decline by around 100 basis points in FY 2027, primarily impacted by the West Asia crisis -related disruptions.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 profit before tax grew 35.7% YoY supported by operating leverage resulting in improved margins
items.quote: In Quarter 1 FY26, our profit before tax grew by 35.7% year -on-year, supported b y operating leverage resulting in improved margins.

items.statement: Research analytics and solutions segment margins expanded to 22.7% in Q1 FY26 from 18.3% in corresponding quarter last year
items.quote: At the profitability level, segment profit increased by 66.9% year-on-year, with margins expanding to 22.7% compared to 18.3% in the corresponding quarter last year.

items.statement: Full year 2025 segment margins improved to 22% for research analytics and solutions segment
items.quote: Looking at the 2025 full year performance for this segment, revenues grew 9.4% year-on-year to INR2,572.4 crores, with segment profit increasing by 12.6% and margins improving to 22%.

items.statement: Rating services segment grew about 20.2% YoY in Q1 2026 supported by strong traction in surveillance fees and new ratings revenues
items.quote: Overall, the rating services segment grew by about 20.2% on Y-o-Y basis in the first quarter of 2026.

items.statement: India mutual fund industry AUM increased from INR55 lakh crores in Q1 2024 to about INR83 lakh crores in Q4 2026
items.quote: The industry AUM increased from INR55 lakh crores in Q1 2024 to about INR83 lakh crores in Q4 2026, as you can see in the chart.

items.statement: Capacity utilization sustained at about 74% in FY26, capex in core manufacturing unlikely to become broad-based near-term given global headwinds
items.quote: Lastly, when we look at the utilization that has sustained at about 74% in FY26, with capex in core manufacturing such as steel and cement, it is unlikely to become broad -based in the near-term given the global headwinds and uncertainty.

items.statement: Emerging sectors such as electronics, semiconductors, batteries, EV manufacturing alongside select traditional sectors will continue to drive capex
items.quote: Emerging sectors such as electronics and components, semiconductors, batteries, and EV manufacturing alongside select traditional sectors will continue to drive capex.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 includes foreign exchange gain of INR14.4 crores compared to loss of INR5.2 crores in same quarter last year
items.quote: Quarter 1 FY26 includes a foreign exchange gain of INR14.4 crores compared to a loss of INR5.2 crores in the first quarter of the corresponding quarter last year.

items.statement: Accelerated closure of renewals in one global business led to incremental revenues of approximately USD4.5 million in Q1 FY26, largely a timing effect expected to normalize
items.quote: Second, I think the accelerated closure of renewals in one of our global businesses has led to incremental revenues of approximately USD4.5 million in quarter 1 FY26 when compared to the same quarter of last year.

items.statement: Launched several pioneering Gen-AI products in 2025 including GenEye Credit, DeepMind, Crisil i360, ICON, and Myron AI low-code solution
items.quote: Some of the Gen -AI native products such as GenEye Credit, which automates credit report creation, DeepMind for intelligent loan data extraction, Crisil i360, a unified intelligence platform offering a macro to micro view across economy, industries, companies and projects, and ICON, an AI-first end-to-end credit workflow management tool, are examples of how we are productizing AI where our domain

items.statement: Serve 11,400-plus clients in 40 countries globally including India's leading banks, NBFCs, majority of top AMCs, and most global corporate investment banks
items.quote: We serve 11,400 -plus clients in 40 countries globally, including India's leading banks, NBFCs, majority of the top AMCs, and most of the global corporate investment banks around the world.

items.statement: Bank credit growth figures from December 2025 onwards not strictly comparable due to change in reporting norms by RBI
items.quote: A small caveat to note is that the bank credit growth figures from December 2025 onwards are not strictly comparable on a like -to-like basis with prior periods due to change in reporting ended by RBI.

items.statement: Sharp INR appreciation against USD will have negative impact on margins, robust forex hedging process in place to counter negative movements
items.quote: Sharp INR appreciation against the USD will have a negative impact on margins. We have a robust forex hedging process to counter negative movements of foreign exchange rates, and we will continue to monitor forex very closely.

items.statement: India Inc deleveraged meaningfully from FY20 to FY25, aggregate net debt to EBITDA improving for sample of 900-plus listed companies forming 55% of listed market cap
items.quote: India Inc deleveraged meaningfully from FY20 to FY25, with aggregate net debt to EBITDA improving for a sample of 900 -plus listed companies, which almost form 55% of the listed market cap.

items.statement: Gross NPA ratios declined from 7.5% in FY21 to about 2% by FY26, expected to remain in check at about 2% to 2.5% by end of March 2027
items.quote: However, the overall system resilience remains strong and banks are expected to keep their gross NPAs in check at about 2% to 2.5% by the end of March 2027 compared with a historical low of an estimated 2% as of March '26.

items.statement: Bond issuances growth flattish in calendar year 2025, declined 12% YoY in Q1 2026 due to West Asia conflict and hardening yields
items.quote: In Q1 2026, the bond issuances declined by 12% on Y -o-Y basis. The West Asia conflict, which began during the quarter, heightened the global macroeconomic uncertainties, which negatively impacted the business sentiments.

items.statement: 5,000-plus experienced professionals, majority of workforce using AI and AI-enabled workflows, certified Great Place to Work in India for sixth consecutive year
items.quote: Finally, our people remain our most valuable intellectual capital. 5,000-plus experienced professionals, their deep domain expertise, amplified by our growing digital foundation, enables us to turn data into actionable insights and measurable impact.

items.statement: Board declared interim dividend of INR9 per share in Q1 FY26 compared to INR8 per share in same quarter last year
items.quote: On shareholder returns, I would also like to highlight that the Board declared an interim dividend of INR9 per share in quarter 1 FY26 compared to INR8 per share in the same quarter last year.

items.statement: Completed acquisition of PriceMetrix, a Toronto-based organization, to enhance wealth management capabilities, Q1 FY26 reflects full quarter of PriceMetrix income
items.quote: We've added a new geography, Canada, followed by our acquisition of PriceMetrix, a Toronto -based organization. And this strategic addition enhances our wealth management capabilities in this imp ortant space of wealth, which is growing.

items.statement: GAC margin profile remains similar as incremental business is similar profile of work to ratings
items.quote: No, see we are doing similar profile of work, so the margin profile remains to be similar.

items.statement: Opened West Asia and Middle East markets; evaluating growth in private markets and regional banks in US, Europe and globally
items.quote: I mean, like I mentioned we have grown, we've opened up the West Asia market, the Middle East market specifically. We are also evaluating growth in the private markets, we're trying to drive growth in regionals, both in US and Europe and around the globe.

items.statement: Credit growth for FY27 expected around 13%, similar to FY26; March numbers indicate potential upside
items.quote: From our side, we believe we've already put this number in public domain that credit growth for the financial year 2027 is going to be around 13%, which is more or less the same what we saw in 2026.

items.statement: Bond market softness due to hardened yields; bank loan market strong in Q1, particularly March
items.quote: If I look at last couple of quarters in bond market, there is softness because yields have hardened. And at this point, it is a little difficult to say by when yield will soften because the geopolitical situation continues to evolve.

items.statement: Substitution of bonds by bank loans due to excess bank liquidity and favourable interest rate differential; no structural change expected medium-term
items.quote: So, if I look at this juncture, what we're seeing is some level of substitution of bonds by bank loans because banks are flushed with liquidity. And if you look at interest rate differential that is prevailing in the bond market versus bank loan, relatively f avouring the bank loan at this point of time

items.statement: RAS segment comprises Global Coalition Greenwich, Integral IQ, and India intelligence business; no individual revenue breakdown disclosed
items.quote: The big parts of that business are the two global businesses, which is the Global Coalition Greenwich business and the Integral IQ business. They are two material parts of that division and of that segment and then followed by the intelligence business in India.

items.statement: Strong Q1 ratings revenue growth driven by robust surveillance revenue from prior-year new ratings and continued investor preference for best-in-class ratings
items.quote: So, if you look at the revenue growth, it is largely driven by a pretty robust surveillance revenue, and also to an extent by new rating revenues. When it comes to surveillance revenue, in general, it is driven by the new rating revenues performance in pr ior year

items.statement: Pricing is complex with no particular 5-year trend; work on pricing in a disciplined manner to cover inflation and sustain margins
items.quote: Pricing is fairly you know, I'll say a complex subject depends on time to time how the situation in the market, etcetera. That decides, I mean there's no particular trend that I can share with you for the last 5 years.

items.statement: Evaluate inorganic opportunities in core and adjacent spaces to accelerate strategy; examples include PriceMetrix acquisition for wealth and stake in SME platform company
items.quote: We continue to evaluate inorganic across the spaces that we operate and the adjacent spaces, and I spoke about some of them as already articulated in our balance sheet. So, wherever we can accelerate our strategy, wherever we can get better capabilities to help us accelerate our strategy, can maybe help us get newer client segments on our current businesses that we have.

items.statement: Adding headcount evenly across businesses for growth investments in technology, Gen-AI, client development and other areas
items.quote: We continue to add people across our businesses as we kind of invest in both growth across technology, Gen -AI, as well as around client development and other areas where we believe those investments are necessary to continue to grow the franchise.

items.statement: No adverse impact from discretionary spend pressure; some decision-making delays but no project cancellations; diversification offsets discretionary spend discussions
items.quote: On the discretionary spend side, what we have seen, and I think I mentioned this earlier that we continue to see engagement from all our clients across all our businesses, including global businesses. And I think the only impact, if at all, I would say is maybe in terms of decision making. In some places, you might see that there could be more time that one might take while taking decisions, but w

items.statement: GCCs viewed as opportunity; partner effectively for COE models and regulatory remediation scaling
items.quote: For us GCC has always been an opportunity as well because GCCs do need support whenever they set up their COE models or where there are regulatory remediations that they have to scale up for at quick notice. GCCs have offered opportunities and we've partnered very effectively with them and that's how we see them in the past 2 years in terms of our overall strategy.

items.statement: Gen-AI embedded across all functions and businesses as opportunity; launched Gen-AI enabled products, enhanced efficiency in services, leveraging domain expertise for regulated financial services clients
items.quote: We stay closely aligned to what our client requirements are. And as adoption accelerates, we also try to evolve our offerings accordingly. I think Amish has already spoken about the fact that we have initiatives across all our functions, as well as all our businesses, whether it is functions like client business development and sales, or whether it is technology, where we have launched Gen -AI ena

items.statement: Accelerated renewal closures in benchmarking business in Q1 will smooth seasonality in subsequent quarters for RAS segment
items.quote: I think this year we've been able to close contracts which typically we would close in subsequent quarters in prior years in the first quarter itself. So, you're right, this will very much have an impact of smoothing in subsequent quarters and some of the seasonality that you've been used to seeing in the RAS segment should hopefully normalize to some extent.

items.statement: No forward-looking statements made; recommend looking at annual performance for better perspective on growth
items.quote: I would first caveat saying that we don't make any forward-looking statements, so I think that is something that I would want you to keep in perspective.

items.statement: Focus on driving growth and sustaining margins across all businesses while leveraging Gen-AI as key differentiator
items.quote: I would like to just say that the focus of the organization is to continue to drive growth and sustain margins, I think that's something across all our businesses is what drives us, while leveraging technology, Gen -AI to be a key differentiator for all our businesses.

items.statement: Management expects loan growth momentum to continue in FY27 but cites geopolitical uncertainty; no specific numeric guidance given.
items.quote: we will continue to have a good momentum and trajectory in our growth. But you have to keep in mind what the geopolitical situatio n and that fallout is going to be

items.statement: Corporate loan demand seen sustaining across electronics, food processing, auto, renewables, semiconductors and acquisition financing.
items.quote: We do see an opportunity in corporate across sectors , in electronics, food processing, auto, auto ancillaries, the renewable sector and the semiconductors.

items.statement: Retail loan growth has stepped up across wheels, personal loans, business loans and mortgages over the last three quarters.
items.quote: Our retail growth has certainly stepped up from where we were last year. And we have seen a better step -up if you've followed our results in the last 3 quarters.

items.statement: NIM trajectory depends on rate cycle and deposit mix; management focuses on ROA stability through cost and credit levers rather than NIM alone.
items.quote: It depends on how the geopolitical situation settles. And so thereby, country's liquidity and borrowing needs, depending on how the oil prices settle, will determine our trajectory of the NIM.

items.statement: Cost of funds at ~4.4%, down ~50 bps YoY; residual repricing of time deposits (5-6 quarters) may reduce cost further if rates stay unchanged.
items.quote: The cost of funds, which is about 4.4% or so, marginally come down. And then from last year to this year, I think so far, it has come down by 50 basis points or so.

items.statement: Borrowings declined ~11% YoY; if borrowings fall to 6-7% of liabilities with all else equal, NIM would improve significantly.
items.quote: If all else remaining same, that means no other factors play in, borrowing percentage coming down will change the NIM trajectory upwards and all else on the other side also remaining same will boost the returns.

items.statement: System credit growth for FY26 estimated at 13.5-13.9% (RBI period-end data), above earlier 10.5-11.5% expectation.
items.quote: When you compare the period -end numbers as of 31st March, which is published by the Reserve Bank of India and you make the math, it comes to somewhere around 13.5% to 13.9%.

items.statement: Bank's loan growth 12% in FY26 vs 5.5% in FY25; deposit growth 14.4% in FY26.
items.quote: We had estimated the system credit growth to be around 10.5% to 11.5%. We did 12%, up from 5.5% last year.

items.statement: ROA stable at 1.9% for FY26; cost-to-income improved to 39.5% from 40.5% on core basis.
items.quote: Despite the drop in NIMs, the return on assets continue to be stable at 1.9% due to cost efficiencies with cost -to-income declining from 40.5% to 39.5% on a core basis.

items.statement: LCR target range 110-120%; currently at 114% (down from 116% last quarter).
items.quote: Our endeavor for LCR is to be between 110% and 120%. We are somewhere in the middle. Last quarter, I think we were about 116%. Now we are 114%.

items.statement: Granular deposits (<₹3 cr) share of incremental net accretion rose from 31% in FY25 to 47% in FY26; retail deposits remain 80-85% of total.
items.quote: The less than INR 3 crores deposits have grown, which has been mobilized in 2026 on a net basis, has grown up almost about 74% over the net incremental deposits for FY25 on that less than INR 3 crores bucket.

items.statement: Merger synergies: home loan liability penetration up from 36% to 50-65%; CASA balances from inherited book grew from ₹50k cr to ₹86k cr in 2.5 years.
items.quote: At that point in time, we roughly had about INR 50,000 crores value of the CASA balances. We have today grown that to INR 86,000 crores.

items.statement: Cost-to-assets ~1.9%, considered best-in-class; cost growth ~6.5-7% YoY, below top-line growth.
items.quote: Cost to assets is at about 1.9 or so. We do think that the cost to asset at 1.9 is best-in-class.

items.statement: Government, RBI and SEBI gave unequivocal support during recent events; legal review in process; NCDRC order found complainants were informed high-risk investors.
items.quote: The Government of India, the Reserve Bank of India and SEBI came out with statements in favor of the bank. The legal review, which is what we had committed at the time when we went to the press, is in process.

items.statement: Geopolitical uncertainty may affect corporate demand for a couple of months; rate cycle paused, securities yields hardening.
items.quote: We will have to temper it given the fallout of what we see in the geopolitical area, which hopefully should not be more than a couple of months going into this financial year.

items.statement: AI platform built in-house with 5 use cases in production, 14 in development; independent risk unit for governance.
items.quote: We already have 5 use cases in production and 14 more in development, improving turnaround times, first-time right outcomes, and freeing mid-office and back-office capacity for customer-facing roles.

items.statement: Third-party distribution fee growth modest at ~3.5% YoY due to tepid volumes and unfavorable product mix; mid-single-digit penetration leaves large opportunity.
items.quote: The third-party products revenue growth has been modest. Both of those components, which is the volume growth, has also been modest. It's positive, but modest given that, whatever preferences the customers have.

items.statement: Treasury/FX income modest due to lower volumes and spreads from foreign exchange trade risks and unwinding impact.
items.quote: There is some negative impact. If you see that the rate of growth on the treasury income is modest. And the reason for that being modest is that , I'm talking about the FX component of the treasury.

items.statement: MSME/business banking grew ~20% YoY; bank #1 in 15 of 28 states, top 2 in 25 states; expects 18-21% growth in FY27.
items.quote: we have grown our business banking, which is mainly representative of our MSME, we've grown at about 20% year -on-year, and that will continue to also be in that range of 18% to 20%, 21

items.statement: Management expects higher single-digit revenue growth for FY27, not double-digit as previously hoped
items.quote: I think for us overall, we might be looking at a single digit, higher single digit growth for the financial year. We may not look at a double-digit growth.

items.statement: Automotive vertical exit growth expected at high-single digit for FY27, not double-digit
items.quote: Having said that, I think maybe we would look at a high-single digit exit, may not get into a double-digit for automotive.

items.statement: Targeting exit PBT margin of ~27% by Q4 FY27
items.quote: I think the idea is that if we can exit the next financial year somewhere near to 27% kind of a margin, not for the full year, but maybe for the exit of this financial year Q4.

items.statement: Healthcare vertical declined 13.1% QoQ CC due to deal delays; expects recovery in Q1 FY27 as deals closed in new quarter
items.quote: I think I'm pretty hopeful that last quarter, Q4, was the bottom and we will be able to recover this. If we had closed these deals earlier in the quarter, then we would have had a fantastic exit to Q4.

items.statement: Transportation revenue grew 0.2% QoQ CC; won two strategic deals from new-age OEM in APAC and next-gen mobility services in US
items.quote: In our transportation business, our revenues in Q4 FY '26 grew by 0.2% quarter -on-quarter in constant currency terms. We are delighted with two strategic wins, one in the APAC region from a new -age OEM and another from a next -generation mobility services company in the US.

items.statement: Media & Communications grew 5.6% QoQ CC led by deal ramp-ups, strategic AdTech deal, Tier 1 US Telco, and multi-year large deal from world-leading device OEM
items.quote: I am happy to report that our Media and Communication business posted a 5.6% quarter -on-quarter revenue growth in constant currency terms. This growth was led by continued deal ramp-ups, a strategic deal for AdTech and a Tier 1 US Telco.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved 130 bps QoQ to 24.6% driven by 155 bps currency tailwind, 65 bps operating efficiencies, offset by 90 bps salary hike impact
items.quote: For the quarter, our EBITDA margin stood at 24.6%, improving by 130 basis points sequentially. This reflects a continued focus on operational excellence and margin improvement.

items.statement: Margin walk: 155 bps from currency, 65 bps from operating leverage, -90 bps from salary hikes = net 130 bps improvement
items.quote: So if I have to put in terms of the margin walk, probably 150-155 basis points is coming from the currency movements against most of the cross -currencies has improved compared to the INR. 65 basis points would have come from the operating efficiencies across different levers that is into play. items.statement: Utilization at 73%; can scale to 80-82% before significant headcount additions needed

items.statement: OEM customers now represent 77% of transportation revenue, up from previous levels
items.quote: I think today we are looking at about 77% of our revenues, 77% of the automotive revenues coming from OEM.

items.statement: Fixed-price contracts increasing but management cautious about shifting too aggressively due to execution risk
items.quote: So, it is not advisable that we continue to shift more and more of our business to fixed price. So, I think that is a careful decision that we need to take because the entire processes in the organization, the SMEs that we have -- the architects that we have.

items.statement: New customers contribute 2-2.5% of revenue per quarter; recent wins include Terumo (Healthcare), APAC new-age OEM (Transportation), and multi-year deal with existing device OEM (Media)
items.quote: I think if you look at it in any quarter, the new customers would contribute maybe 2% to 2.5% of the revenue. items.statement: New logo ramp-up typically takes 9-12 months to deliver significant revenue impact
items.quote: Usually, even if you win a deal, for it to make a significant impact, it takes anywhere between 9 months to 12 months for ramp -ups to actually happen and start delivering.

items.statement: AI/GenAI driving both internal efficiency and pricing power; customers in Media/Telecom demanding efficiency gains, while Auto/Healthcare focus on regulatory compliance and value
items.quote: It's both. Definitely, we are using a lot of that for internal efficiencies. However, there are customers that are demanding better efficiencies, productivity and so on, which automatically leads to, if you're able to deliver that performance and productivity, then a better pricing power. So it's a combination of both.

items.statement: No broad irrational pricing from competitors despite GenAI; few aggressive bids but unclear if GenAI-driven; customers cautious about full GenAI-based solutions
items.quote: No, I don't think we have seen irrationality in general, right? Because see, ER&D is still a very, very specialized -- it is not that we can use AI or GenAI across the board, right? So having said that, yes, we have seen a few contracts where there has been competition that has priced very, very aggressively, and we are also a little bit surprised.

items.statement: Revenue INR 993.8 crore in Q4 FY26, up 0.9% QoQ in constant currency
items.quote: I am pleased to announce that we have delivered a healthy revenue of INR993.8 crores for the quarter, growing 0.9% quarter-on-quarter in constant currency terms.

items.statement: Healthcare & Life Sciences revenue declined 13.1% QoQ in constant currency
items.quote: Our Healthcare and Life Sciences vertical de- grew by 13.1% quarter -on-quarter in constant currency terms, impacted by delays in deal awards that we were expecting and prepared for in the quarter.

items.statement: Transportation revenue grew 0.2% QoQ in constant currency
items.quote: In our transportation business, our revenues in Q4 FY '26 grew by 0.2% quarter -on-quarter in constant currency terms.

items.statement: Media & Communications revenue grew 5.6% QoQ in constant currency
items.quote: I am happy to report that our Media and Communication business posted a 5.6% quarter -on-quarter revenue growth in constant currency terms.

items.statement: Geopolitical uncertainty and tariff wars creating deal delays and elongated decision cycles; both deal wins and push-outs occurring simultaneously
items.quote: We are seeing both sides, right? We have also announced deals that we have won in the quarter. We also know that there are cases where the deals have been pushed off. So, there is no one answer to your question, right? It is, both are happening.

items.statement: Incubating new verticals: Aerospace & Defense (working with HAL, ADA, global players), Battery Energy Storage (for data centers/EVs), and Manufacturing; expects one or two to show results in 4-6 quarters
items.quote: We've also started focusing a little bit on the manufacturing side. We've built certain capabilities, we've won some initial customers. That is another area we continue to invest.

items.statement: Opened offshore development center for Terumo Corporation (Japanese MedTech leader) for cardiac and vascular solutions
items.quote: However, during the quarter, we opened an offshore development center for the Japanese MedTech leader Terumo Corporation. This center brings together the power of design, engineering and digital to innovate their cardiac and vascular solutions.

items.statement: Launched automotive SDLC platform DevStudio.ai in Q4 FY26; building AI-native engineering organization with curated tool stacks, agent inventory, sandbox environments, and upskilling
items.quote: In FY '26, we significantly advanced our adoption of GenAI. This was supported by partnerships with AI companies, launch of our own automotive SDLC platform DevStudio.ai earlier in this quarter, curated tool stacks and agent inventory, investments in infrastructure, sandbox environments with IP protection and data pr ivacy, and rigorous upskilling.

items.statement: Aspire to be top three in India's ILCV trucks and buses segment with focus play in HCVs
items.quote: During the Global Investor Day in November 2025, we had set announced our aspiration that In Mahindra, trucks and buses businesses, both brands combined, we aspire to be top three in India's ILCV trucks and buses segment, intermediate and light commercial vehicle buses and trucks segment with focus play in HCVs.

items.statement: Targeting 10-12% combined market share by FY31 from current 6%
items.quote: we are looking at a market share aspiration of 10 to 12% with both brands combined presence, which right now is at 6 and we are very much planning and working towards that.

items.statement: Targeting around 15,000 crores revenue by FY31
items.quote: See, in the Global Investor Day, we did mention that around FY31, we are talking targeting 15,000 crores.

items.statement: No major demand concern currently; peak school bus season plans unchanged but diesel price hike could temporarily impact demand
items.quote: What we are seeing today is, in spite of all the challenges which we have around so far, we don't see any major concern as far as demand situation is concerned.

items.statement: Industry grew 22% in H2 FY26 post-GST reform with ICV trucks up 42%, LCV trucks 20%, MCV trucks 28%
items.quote: If I give you some figures, within that, ICV trucks had 42 percent growth, LCV trucks had 20 percent, MCV trucks has 28 percent, and ILCV was at 8 percent growth.

items.statement: Q4 saw 1.3% commodity cost increase (annualized 3.5-3.7%); price hikes of 2-3% taken from April 15
items.quote: So on in quarter four, we saw around 1.3 percent increase, which at annualised level would be around 3.5 to 3.7 percent.

items.statement: Price increases of 2-3% implemented from April 15 to offset commodity inflation
items.quote: We have already taken a price increase starting from 15th of April, which for SML products, mostly it is around 2 percent and, in some cases, we have taken 3 percent price increase.

items.statement: Significant cost increases in steel, aluminium, copper, polymers and gases due to geopolitical disruption; most believed temporary
items.quote: Things like steel started moving up even before war, but post that we have seen further increase in that. Aluminium we have seen in phase, copper we have seen in phase, polymers we have seen in phase.

items.statement: Pre-poned institutional cargo orders to Q3 to free capacity for Q4 school bus season; gained 170 bps bus market share in Q4
items.quote: we executed large number of institutional orders in quarter three itself as a preparation for season of school buses in quarter four, where the large capacity gets booked in quarter four.

items.statement: Launched 3 products in 8 months: advanced life support ambulance, 15-18 seat AC bus for maxi cab, front overhang AC bus
items.quote: We launched three products in the last eight months. One was advanced life care support ambulance, which is doing quite well.

items.statement: First electric bus launch planned in FY27; hydrogen fuel cells seen as future for heavy trucks
items.quote: in this financial year itself, we'll be launching that. Post that, we will evaluate every opportunity on the merit of its commercial viability and returns and we will take the appropriate call, just to repeat towards the in this financial year itself, we are going to launch our first EV bus and we will enter into this segment.

items.statement: Cross-badging strategy for unrepresented territories; common dealers appointed where neither brand present
items.quote: Wherever there is, there are territories both where both the both the brands don't have a presence, then it's obvious case that we will appoint a common dealer which will now we have a higher probability of getting because both brands put together is providing higher potential for looking at dealers in some of this unrepresented territory.

items.quote: In the 3 1/2 tonne plus segment with Mahindra Truck and versus segment last year, the whole industry revenue pool was 125,000 crores, 1.25 lakh crores, and we have got 6 to 7 percent market share out of that.

items.quote: there is a ADAS regulation which has been announced which CV industry has to get ready with and within the next 1 1/2 years.

items.quote: as far as your question related to delisting of SML is concerned, the clear answer to that is no.

items.quote: Typical things like medical policy of SML employees have been brought in line with the Mahindra medical policy. All of them, all of that 6 has gone down very, very well with SML employees who now are part of Mahindra larger ecosystem and feel proud to be working with us together

items.quote: volume growth for cargo vehicle was 10% and passengers 16%. Market share, there is a minor blip, but I'll explain.

items.quote: Our revenue was up 18%. PAT was up 31% in the year. And our rating went two notches up from AA minus to AA plus.

items.statement: Q4 revenue up 16%, PAT up 2% despite inflationary pressures
items.quote: for quarter four, our revenue went up by 16%. Our PAT went up by 2%.

items.statement: Geopolitical uncertainty and potential diesel price hike could temporarily impact CV demand; scenario planning in place
items.quote: How the industry will play after quarter one is dependent upon multiple factors, especially in view of the current geopolitical situation. the likely talks about the diesel price increase.

items.statement: Integration completed in record 8 months; SML Mahindra operating as Mahindra Group company with SPA conditions fulfilled
items.quote: in eight months, in the record 8 months after takeover, we have already managed to integrate the business. SML Mahindra is operating like any other Mahindra Group Company as we speak.

items.statement: Management expects FY27 to be a positive growth year, growing faster than FY26, but maintains a cautiously positive stance due to macro and AI-led pricing uncertainty.
items.quote: We believe that FY27 will be a positive growth year, should grow faster than FY26.

items.statement: Management does not provide specific revenue guidance but expects FY27 performance to be better than FY26.
items.quote: So Ankur, usually, we don't give guidance on future numbers. Having said that, we believe it will be a better performance than the previous year.

items.statement: Management targets stable EBITDA margin of 16%-16.1% for FY27, balancing AI-led efficiency gains against pricing pressure and AI investments.
items.quote: As we have stated earlier, Ankur, we believe maintaining margin percentage for the coming period at 16% -16.1% is where we see the margin performances.

items.statement: 12-month order backlog reached $300.4 million, up 1.5% sequentially and 13.5% YoY in USD (24.4% in INR).
items.quote: We closed the year with 12-month backlog of $300.4 million, a sequential growth of 1.5% and a Y-o-Y growth of 13.5% in USD and 24.4% in INR terms.

items.statement: North America order book grew for the second consecutive quarter with positive lead indicators for continued growth in coming quarters.
items.quote: We've had a second quarter of positive order book growth in North America. And we have good visibility to a strong order book even continuing in the coming quarters.

items.quote: Healthcare and Life Sciences, which is one of our most important sectors, continues to see a very positive demand outlook, although the current performance of this quarter has seen a quarter -on-quarter dip, which is primarily a timing gap between current projects getting executed and new projects getting started.

items.statement: Public sector remains stable with contract renewals providing long-term visibility.
items.quote: As far as the public sector is concerned, which is the backbone of Mastek's growth, it continues to be stable. We've renewed a few more contracts of ours for a good long-term visibility, and we continue to deliver really well.

items.statement: Financial services sector showing strong improvement with two large North American institutions and other wins in UK and AMEA driving revenue and resource ramp-up.
items.quote: The star of the quarter was financial services, and we're starting to see some really good improvement in our financial services sector. items.statement: AI-led deals currently comprise two categories: AI for tech (70-80% AI usage in legacy modernization, testing, managed services) and early-stage AI for business use case deployments.
items.quote: These are AI -led technology deals where we are using AI for delivering newer programs, which are like legacy modernization or AI -led testing or managed services kind of deals. items.statement: FY27 focus shifts significantly towards AI for business with verticalization based on AI as key mantra.
items.quote: Our focus is now shifting significantly towards AI for business as we look at many new programs where we have started delivering some small but very influential AI-led use cases for our clients. As we step into the year, verticalizing the business based on AI is going to be a key mantra for FY '27.

items.statement: Renewals facing 10-15% price discounts due to AI-driven efficiency visibility, with potential for higher discounts; shifting commercial model from T&M to outcome-based fixed bid contracts.
items.quote: Like we had mentioned in our earlier quarters, we had renewed some of our contracts with anywhere around 10% to 15% discount. But depending on the nature of business and the nature of customers, it could go much higher than that as we go into these discussions.

items.statement: Merged two Indian entities (Mastek Enterprise Solutions Private Limited and Mastek Limited) to simplify structure and eliminate duplicate operational and administrative costs.
items.quote: During the year, we merged two entities in India, which is Mastek Enterprise Solutions Private Limited and Mastek Limited. Mastek Enterprise Solutions Private Limited was a wholly owned subsidiary of Mastek Limited. This has been done to simplify the entity structure in India and to el iminate duplicate operational and administrative costs and overheads.

items.statement: Utilization improved to 80% in Q4, up 3.3% from Q3 and 1.7% from Q2; headcount grew by 54 to 4,730.
items.quote: Utilization rate improved during Q4 at 80%, which was an improvement of 3.3% from Q3 and 1.7% from Q2.

items.statement: Headcount growth expected to be slower than revenue growth, driving revenue per resource improvement.

Having said that, a lot of business mix between on -site, offshore, some of the kind of programs may change that. But directionally, the headcount growth should be slower than the revenue growth, and therefore, the revenue per resource should move positively.

items.statement: DSO reduced to 73 days in Q4, the lowest in 12 quarters, driven by strong collections of $125 million.
items.quote: During Q4 of '26, we had a very strong collection quarter from our customers, wherein we collected $125 million, which helped us reduce our DSO to 73. This is the lowest DSO we have had in last 12 quarters.

items.statement: Management aims to maintain DSO at current levels long-term, though short-term fluctuations of a few days are expected.
items.quote: So of course, there will be some variation from where we are today, but our endeavour is to basically maintain the DSO at the level we have reached. items.statement: Declared final dividend of INR16 per share (on top of INR8 interim dividend), totaling 480% of face value.
