items.statement: Credit cost was 38 basis points in FY2026, under 50 bps adjusted
items.quote: The credit cost was 38 basis points in FY2026. Adjusted for the additional standard asset provision in respect of the agricultural priority sector portfolio and corporate recoveries, the credit cost was under 50 basis points in FY2026.

items.statement: Branch count increased by 126 in Q4 and 528 in FY2026 to 7,511 branches
items.quote: Our branch count has increased by 126 in Q4 and 528 in FY2026. We had 7,511 branches as of March 31, 2026.

items.statement: Board recommended dividend of 12 Rupees per share for FY2026
items.quote: The Board has recommended a dividend of 12 Rupees per share for FY2026, subject to requisite approvals.

items.statement: CET-1 ratio 16.35% and total capital adequacy 17.18% at March 31, 2026
items.quote: The capital position of the Bank continued to be strong with a CET-1 ratio of 16.35% and total capital adequacy ratio of 17.18% at March 31, 2026, after reckoning the impact of proposed dividend.

items.statement: Treasury loss of 1.06 billion includes impact of capping FX net open positions per RBI guidelines
items.quote: There was a treasury loss of 1.06 billion Rupees in this quarter as compared to loss of 1.57 billion Rupees in the previous quarter and gain of 2.39 billion Rupees in Q4 of last year primarily reflecting market movements and includes the impact of capping of FX net open positions in the onshore market as per recent RBI guidelines.

items.statement: Mortgage growth driven by benchmark rate stabilization giving space to grow portfolio
items.quote: As the benchmark has settled, it has given us the space to grow that portfolio and that is what you have seen over the last 2 quarters and more particularly in this quarter.

items.statement: West Asia conflict creating uncertainty but bank has strong franchise, capital, funding to grow within risk parameters
items.quote: Of course, more recently, since March, the conflict in West Asia has clouded the outlook in the sense that it has created some amount of uncertainty. But from our side, we believe we have a strong franchise, healthy capital levels and strong funding and liquidity. So, we would want to leverage that to grow the business within our parameters of risk acceptance.

items.statement: Operating expenses grew 12.0% YoY in Q4 and 11.5% YoY in FY2026
items.quote: The Bank's operating expenses increased by 12.0% year-on-year in this quarter and 11.5% year-on-year in FY2026.

items.statement: Aims for opex growth below top-line growth next year
items.quote: And the final numbers on business growth are a little ahead of operating expenses growth, and we hope that, that will be sustained over the next year. So, definitely, we would want to have opex growth at a level which is below the top line growth.

items.statement: ICICI Life APE increased to 106.41 billion Rupees in FY2026 from 104.07 billion in FY2025
items.quote: The annualised premium equivalent of ICICI Life increased to 106.41 billion Rupees in FY2026 from 104.07 billion Rupees in FY2025.

items.statement: ICICI Life VNB margin improved to 24.7% in FY2026 from 22.8% in FY2025
items.quote: The value of new business margin was 24.7% in FY2026 compared to 22.8% in FY2025.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guidance 1-4% constant currency, services 1.5-4.5%, EBIT margin 17.5-18.5%
items.quote: Our guidance for FY'27 is as follows. The revenue growth guidance for the full year is 1% to 4% in constant currency and 1.5% to 4.5% for Services. EBIT margin guidance is 17.5% to 18.5%.

items.statement: Discretionary spending cut by two large US Telecom clients, two SAP programs discontinued, impact to continue through calendar year
items.quote: We expect the impact to continue for rest of the calendar year as well, which is accounted for in the guidance we will provide.

items.statement: Q4 EBIT margin 16.5%, 17.7% excluding restructuring; FY26 EBIT margin 17.2%, 17.9% adjusted
items.quote: Our operating margin for the quarter came at 16.5%, and it would be 17.7%, excluding restructuring costs.

items.statement: Q4 net new bookings TCV $1.9B, FY26 TCV $9.3B flat YoY despite AI deflation
items.quote: TCV of net new bookings for the year clocked $9.3 billion, same as last year, in spite of some of the AI deflation that you see in the TCV net new booking.

items.statement: Advanced AI revenue $155.1M in Q4 (6.1% QoQ), $620M annualized; AI Factory, Physical AI, Custom Silicon Engineering seeing traction
items.quote: Advanced AI revenue for the quarter stood at $155.1 million, marking a 6.1% QoQ growth.

items.statement: Added 1 $100M client, 8 $50M clients, 28 $1M clients in FY26; two US Telecom clients cut discretionary spend
items.quote: If you look at our client categories, we've grown them across the board, starting with an increase of one for clients greater than $100 million, an increase of eight $50 million clients, and all the way at $1 million, we added 28 clients.

items.statement: Investing in AI talent (135K trained in GenAI, 11.8K AI builders, 700+ black belts), hiring lateral talent for AI data center programs
items.quote: To date, we've trained 135,000 employees in GenAI technologies. Additionally, 11,800 AI builders and more than 700-plus black belts for service transformation have been trained and certified.

items.statement: Signed definitive agreement to acquire Finergic Solutions (wealth consulting, Singapore); completed Wobby acquisition (data intelligence AI)
items.quote: We signed a definitive agreement to acquire Finergic Solutions, a boutique wealth consulting firm headquartered in Singapore.

items.statement: Interim dividend INR24/share declared; FY26 payout INR60/share (97.6% of net income); capital allocation policy extended 5 years at minimum 75% payout
items.quote: The Board has declared an interim dividend of INR24 per share for the quarter. The record date is 25th of April '26, and the payment of the same shall be on 5th of May'26.

items.statement: DSO 84 days, up 3 days QoQ; operating cash flow $2.25B, free cash flow $2.09B (115% and 107% of net income)
items.quote: Our DSO is currently at 84 days, increased by three days QoQ.

items.statement: Services ROIC 47% (+155bps YoY), Software ROIC 22.6% (+274bps), Company ROIC 40.3% (+235bps)
items.quote: Services ROIC now is at 47%, up 155 basis points YoY. Software continued to improve with ROIC at 22.6%, up 274 basis points YoY.

items.statement: Two client-specific challenges in Americas create ~50bps growth headwind in FY27; Europe softness; geopolitical uncertainty limits visibility
items.quote: For FY'27, we see a half a percent reduction due to two clients and their own business challenges.

items.statement: AI-driven deflation estimated 2-3% for HCLTech portfolio (vs 3-5% industry); incremental to traditional productivity commitments
items.quote: For us, we called out 2% to 3% and I think that holds true even now.

items.statement: HPE Telecom Solutions Group and Jaspersoft acquisitions delayed due to US government approval delays from department shutdowns
items.quote: This guidance does not include the two acquisitions, the Telecom Solutions Group from HPE that we announced to carve-out and Jaspersoft. Both of these are not closed yet. They are delayed due to the US government approval that's delayed due to the US government shutdown of the specific departments.

items.statement: Forex had positive 65bps impact on Q4 margins; USA grew 4.9% YoY, Europe -2.9%, ROW 16.6%, India 5.3%
items.quote: And forex had a positive impact of 65 basis points.

items.statement: Walking away from hyper-competitive traditional deals; lost voluntary deals worth ~$1B TCV to focus on AI reinvention
items.quote: We have walked away from some deals which will not make sense and that would have easily contributed at least $1 billion more to this number.

items.statement: Q4 revenue $3.682B (-3.3% QoQ, +2.4% YoY CC); Services $3.386B (-0.1% QoQ, +4.2% YoY); Software $307M (-28.1% QoQ, -14.1% YoY)
items.quote: Total revenue for the quarter is $3,682 million, a drop of 3.3% Q oQ, but with a growth of 2.4% YoY in constant currency

items.statement: Targeting loan book growth in line with industry at 13-15% for FY27
items.quote: We do believe that momentum should certainly continue and not just in certain products or segments. I think what we are now talking about is a lot more secular across segments. Of course, Retail Disbursement growth rates are quite aggressive. We're moving fast now, given that we now have confidence on the Asset Quality and Profitability. But having said that, the book is slated to grow in double d

items.statement: Retail loan book growth targeted at 10-11% for FY27
items.quote: But what we are aiming to grow the Retail Book next year is actually should hit the double-digit growth. So, let's say, about 10% to 11% is what we do believe it should deliver.

items.statement: Corporate loan book growth targeted at ~20% for FY27
items.quote: If I look at the Corporate Book, that's already growing at about 20%. So, we do believe we have the levers to grow at 20%.

items.statement: Commercial Banking loan growth targeted at ~18% for FY27
items.quote: Commercial Banking is something that is a space we like. Historically has been a good growth driver for us, and that continues to also deliver about 18% growth.

items.statement: Targeting RIDF reduction of INR 6,500-9,000 crores by end of FY27
items.quote: We've ended this year at about INR 27,900 crores, ballpark INR 28,000 crores. We think that next year, at a minimum, the reduction should be about INR 6,500 crores. That could also go as high as INR 9,000 crores by the end of March '27.

items.statement: RIDF reduction pace similar in FY28 then slows in FY29-30
items.quote: So the reduction of RIDF from here on will -- so for example, FY28 and FY29 will be equally split and then there are some maturities in FY30. So I would say it starts getting thinner in terms of the pace of reduction. So FY28 will be similar to FY27 potentially, but FY29, FY30 will start getting thinner.

items.statement: Structural NIM target of 3.25-3.5% over 2-3 years
items.quote: We've said that structurally over a 3-year period, let's say, now about 2 to 3 year period, we do believe that we will want to get into a 3.25% to 3.5% kind of a range from a margin perspective.

items.statement: Targeting core ROA improvement of 25-50 bps over next 2-3 years excluding JC Flowers write-backs
items.quote: But what we have very emphatically worked upon internally is to say, internal, outside of the JC Flowers ARC write-backs, we will look to improve our ROA 25 to 50 basis points.

items.statement: SR recoveries guidance of INR 800-1,000 crores for FY27
items.quote: In line with the rundown in the face value of the Security Receipts, we expect recoveries to the tune of INR 800 crores to INR 1,000 crores from SRs in FY27.

items.statement: Branch expansion plan of ~80 branches per year for next 4-5 years
items.quote: We had laid out a guidance for the next 4 to 5 years with a plan of around 400 branches with an average of around 80 branches per annum, and we are on course of that.

items.statement: NIM improved 10 bps QoQ and 20 bps YoY to 2.7% in Q4 FY26
items.quote: Despite adverse interest rate environment and elevated competitive intensity in Deposits, our NIM saw an improvement of 10 basis points quarter-on-quarter and 20 basis points year-on-year and came in at a number of 2.7%.

items.statement: Full year FY26 NIM at 2.6%, up 20 bps YoY, in line with guidance
items.quote: Even for the full year, the NIM at 2.6% improved 20 basis points vis-a-vis FY25 and in line with our guidance given in Q4 of FY25.

items.statement: Savings account rate reduced by over 150 bps over last year, now below 4.5%
items.quote: If you look at our Savings Account rate over the last 1 year, we've taken the benefit of this reducing rate cycle to cut our rates by over 150 basis points. So, Savings Account rate, which was blended 6% is now well below 4.5%.

items.statement: Retail disbursements grew ~41% YoY in Q4 FY26
items.quote: Retail disbursements in particular, have gained significant momentum, registering approximately 41% year-on-year growth in Q4FY26.

items.statement: Retail disbursement YoY growth above 20%, expected to normalize at 20-25%
items.quote: So, if you look from a Y-o-Y perspective, in fact, we are kind of way above a 20% Y-o-Y growth. We do believe that it should ultimately get normalized in the 20-25% range.

items.statement: Total advances grew 11.1% YoY to INR 2.73 lakh crores
items.quote: Total Advances registered a growth of 11.1% year-on-year to INR 2.73 lakh crores.

items.statement: Total deposits grew 12.1% YoY to INR 3.18 lakh crores, crossed INR 3 lakh crore milestone
items.quote: While overall Deposits crossed the milestone of INR 3 lakh crores, the CASA balances crossed the milestone of INR 1 lakh crores. Total Deposits increased 12.1% year-on-year to INR 3.18 lakh crores.

items.statement: CASA balances grew 14.9% YoY to INR 1.12 lakh crores, CASA ratio improved to 35.1%
items.quote: CASA balances grew 14.9% year-on- year to INR 1.12 lakh crores. Even on an A verage Quarterly Balance (AQB) basis, the CASA growth was strong at 11.2%. And the CASA ratio also improved 80 basis points year-on-year and 110 basis points Q-o-Q to 35.1

items.statement: Credit-to-Deposit ratio improved to 85.7% from 88% in Q3 FY26
items.quote: Our Credit-to-Deposit (CD) ratio, improved to 85.7% from 88% in Q3FY26 and 86.5% in Q4FY25.

items.statement: GNPA 1.3%, NNPA 0.2% as of March 2026, lowest in 24 quarters
items.quote: As at 31st March '26, the Bank reported Gross NPA and Net NPA ratio of 1.3% and 0.2%, respectively, the lowest ever that we have seen in the last 24 quarters and amongst the top quartile in our peer set.

items.statement: Gross slippage ratio improved to 1.8% in FY26 from 2.1% in FY25
items.quote: Gross slippage ratio in FY26 has improved to 1.8% versus 2.1% last year.

items.statement: Retail asset slippages improved to 3.5% in FY26 from 4% in FY25, Q4 exit rate 2.8%
items.quote: This has been led by improvement in the Retail Asset Slippages, which improved in FY26 to 3.5% from 4% in FY25 with the exit rate even lower at 2.8% in Q4FY26 versus 3.4% the last quarter.

items.statement: Credit card slippages ~INR 135-140 crores, Personal loan slippages down to ~INR 160 crores in Q4 FY26
items.quote: The Credit Card was about INR 133 crores and Personal Loans was about INR 180 crores. So that INR 186 crores Personal Loans is down to about INR 160 crores. And Credit Cards continued to be in the range of about INR 135 to 140 crores.

items.statement: Total recoveries and upgrades INR 4,795 crores in FY26, including INR 1,550 crores from SRs
items.quote: The Bank had total Recoveries and Upgrades of INR 4,795 crores in FY26, which included recoveries from Security Receipts (SRs) of a little more than INR 1,550 crores against our guidance of INR 1,200 crores.

items.statement: Provision Coverage Ratio healthy at 81.9%
items.quote: Further, the Provision Coverage Ratio (PCR) continues to remain healthy at 81.9%.

items.statement: Credit costs low at 0.2% for FY26 and 0.17% for Q4 FY26
items.quote: Overall Credit Costs remained low at 0.2% for the full year FY26 versus 0.3% last year. Credit Cost for the Q4FY26 was at 0.17%.

items.statement: Cost-to-Income ratio improved to 66.7% for FY26 from 71.3% in FY25, Q4 exit at 63%
items.quote: Cost-to-Income Ratio for FY26 also saw a big improvement to 66.7% versus 71.3% in FY25. That's 66.7% now versus 71.3% last year. The exit for the financial year came in even lower with the Cost-to-Income Ratio coming at 63% vis-a-vis 66.1% Q3 FY26 and 67.3% the same quarter last year.

items.statement: Non-interest income to average assets ratio improved to 1.5% in FY26 from 1.1% in FY23
items.quote: Over the last three years, the Bank has seen a meaningful increase in its Non-interest Income to Average Assets Ratio, which has increased from 1.1% in FY23 to 1.5% this year FY26.

items.statement: PPOP grew 29.4% YoY to INR 5,506 crores in FY26, PPOP to average assets 1.2%
items.quote: For FY26, the Bank had a Pre-Provisioning Operating Profit (PPOP) of INR 5,506 crores, which grew 29.4% year-on-year. FY26 PPOP as a percentage to Average Total Assets improved to 1.2% versus 1% for FY25 and 0.9% in FY24.

items.statement: Appointed S. Anantharaman as Chief Risk Officer with over three decades of experience
items.quote: I'm pleased to welcome on Board Mr. S. Anantharaman as the Chief Risk Officer of the Bank. He is an industry veteran with over three decades of experience with rich experience, rich expertise in the risk management domain.

items.statement: AT1 bonds case subjudice, hearings completed at Supreme Court, judgment reserved
items.quote: on the AT1 matter, this matter is subjudice, as you all know. The hearings have taken place at the Supreme Court, and the matter is also reserved for judgment. We will wait to hear from the Supreme Court -- Honorable Supreme Court on the verdict

items.statement: Proactively monitoring MSME portfolio for West Asia conflict impact, no stress signs yet
items.quote: We are proactively monitoring our portfolio, and this is the exercise that we've already started. It's good to report that all our clients, whether it's an MSME or larger clients have been managing well. They have not shown any signs of stress.

items.statement: Yield on advances ~9.2% as of March 2026 exit
items.quote: For yield on advances that we've had as we look to exit March, that has been about 9.2%.

items.statement: AFS reserve negative balance ~INR 100 crores as of March 31, swing of ~INR 200 crores
items.quote: The AFS reserve, we have a negative balance of about INR 100 crores as of March 31. The swing would be about INR 200 crores.

items.statement: Made INR 341 crores proactive standard asset provisioning in Q4 FY26, not reflecting credit issues
items.quote: And we did realize that there are sometimes evolving and possibly even prudent provisioning policies. And that application we have done in quarter 4 of this year, which translates to about INR 341 crores. I want to be emphatically clear here that the provisioning that we have done on certain, let's say, product or segments in no way reflect an underlying credit issue or an impairment or our view a

items.statement: FY26 year-end unexecuted order book at 2.83 GWp, down from 3.2 GWp a year earlier
items.quote: For the year-end our unexecuted order book stood at 2.83 gigawatt peak, providing us with strong visibility and continuity of business going forward.

items.statement: Order pipeline of ~36 GWp being pursued, split ~23 GWp domestic and ~12 GWp international
items.quote: Apart from that, we are also chasing the order pipeline of around 36 gigawatt, which is around 23 gigawatt is from domestic and maybe another 12 gigawatt from the international market.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin 19.24%; management guides a 15% threshold but expects operational efficiency to sustain higher levels
items.quote: So, if you will see on a year-on-year basis also, we have more or less, we have able to achieve similar kind of margin. So maybe in a particular quarter, you may see some slightly different, but overall basis from last FY25 as well as FY26 also, we are more than 19%.

items.statement: Management says 15% EBITDA margin is a guiding threshold, not a ceiling; expects discipline to keep margins above that
items.quote: So it is not that it will get neutralized at this kind of percentage. Going forward also like whatever order we have executed, the operational efficiency and discipline execution, timely execution, all this process will play and this will keep on improving, maybe going forward also.

items.statement: IPP capex funded internally; ~200 MWp under construction at INR3-3.5 crore per MWp
items.quote: So capex is, suppose, I will give you the rough number for any kind of solar capacity which you want to install. If you put anything between it, it comes to INR3 crores to INR3.5 crores per megawatt peak.

items.statement: No debt tied up for IPP projects; funded through internal accruals only
items.quote: So far, we have not tied up any kind of debt for this. We are funding it internally.

items.statement: Q4 revenue mix ~50% with-module orders; order book composition ~20% with-module, rest pure EPC/BOS
items.quote: So, for this quarter actually, around, if I say any rough idea is around 50% of the execution revenue numbers are coming from with module.

items.statement: Order book realization range INR1-1.25 crore per MWp depending on scope
items.quote: So, it is broadly this range in between INR1 crores to INR1.25 crores or INR1.2 crores megawatt.

items.statement: India added >44 GW solar in FY26 vs 23.8 GW in FY25; solar ~82% of renewable additions
items.quote: In FY '2026, over 44 gigawatt of solar capacity was added, representing a substantial increase from 23.83 gigawatt in the previous year.

items.statement: FY26 execution 2,727 MWp, highest ever; order book execution timeline 12-15 months
items.quote: During FY '2026, we have successfully executed 2,727 megawatt peak of projects, which is highest for any year.

items.statement: O&M portfolio 1.18 GWp at FY26 end, providing recurring revenue base
items.quote: At the same time, our O&M portfolio stood at 1.18 gigawatt peak, further strengthening our base of recurring revenue and reinforcing our role as a reliable long-term partner for our customers.

items.statement: Module cost pass-through on turnkey orders; no margin impact from ALCM/DCR price changes
items.quote: So, for Waaree Renewable Technologies, there is like nothing, even if it goes up also, it is passed through to the customer.

items.statement: Receivables mostly <6 months, many secured by LCs; no significant payment stretch from customers
items.quote: No, mostly our most of our receivables are less than 6 months only. And in many of the contracts, we are secured by way of letter of credits also.

items.statement: Inventory tied to specific project requirements; will be billed subsequently
items.quote: So inventory whatever inventory we are procuring, whatever components we are offering, mostly almost all are for the specific project requirements only.

items.statement: Company remains asset-light with no significant debt for IPP projects
items.quote: As you rightly said, we are the asset light company and we are not carrying any significant debt in our books as of now for these projects.

items.statement: IPP operational capacity 54 MWp generating INR26 crore revenue in FY26; additional 227 MWp under construction
items.quote: So, we have current around 54 megawatts of IPP assets which are running and generating revenue. The revenue is around INR26 crores for this financial year.

items.statement: BESS EPC inquiries increasing; executing one small BESS project in FY27; no data center revenue yet
items.quote: However, we are executing one of the BESS project, relatively smaller size, but we are executing during this quarter or maybe this financial year.

items.statement: Order book geographically concentrated in Rajasthan; also executing in Gujarat, MP, Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra
items.quote: Majority of the that in those areas, but other areas also significantly equally significantly like Maharashtra and MP and Andhra is also contributing a great amount of orders.

items.statement: No regulatory hurdles for project execution; permissions already in place for awarded orders
items.quote: No, as such, there is no regulatory requirement because the permission which are necessary for the installation of solar projects is already in place.

items.statement: Rajasthan evacuation backlog (60 GW awaiting substation clarity) seen as developer risk; EPC orders awarded only after studies done
items.quote: So by that time this backlog will be there. There is an always risk which is taken by the developer when they know that these are the power evacuation and when they are likely to be in place.

items.statement: Participates in tenders only when margin and risk-reward metrics are met; bilateral pipeline conversion expected
items.quote: But as Waaree, as a company, we are only participating when it is suitable to our margin or suitable to risk reward metrics, which we prefer.

items.statement: No overseas EPC execution yet; pursuing international pipeline of ~12 GWp
items.quote: As of now, we are not executing anything, sir. But we have this pipeline or in pipeline, which we are chasing for the overseas projects also.

items.statement: No management changes or headcount details discussed
items.quote: Today on the call, I have along with me the key members of our management team.

items.statement: No dividend or buyback announcements made
items.quote: We now open the floor for any questions you may have.

items.statement: Domestic supply chain for all components; no direct impact from global oil/gas or raw material inflation
items.quote: So, from the current situation, which is prevailing in the world. So, indirectly, everybody is impacted, actually, in one or the other form. But as far as the company is concerned, we are, we have all domestic orders and all domestic supply chains.

items.statement: FY26 revenue INR3,331.42 crore (+108.5% YoY), EBITDA INR641.10 crore (+106.2% YoY), PAT INR478.65 crore (+109.1% YoY)
items.quote: For the financial year 2026, we reported revenue of INR3,331.42 crores, a growth of 108.51% over FY2025. EBITDA stood at INR641.10 crores, up 106.21% year-on-year basis. While PAT reached INR478.65 crores, showing growth of 109.09% on year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Marketing spend (cost to grow) stable at INR 450-500 cr annually; Q1 FY27 slightly higher due to IPL
items.quote: If you look at between last year and this year we would have spent very similar to INR450 crores to INR500 crores is kind of spend. And we will keep on increasing this a little bit, but it's not going to be again linear with terms of revenue.

items.statement: Cost to operate (Groww platform) to rise in Q1 FY27 due to appraisals, then stabilize in absolute terms; AMC and Fisdom costs will rise further
items.quote: With the exception of these risk related costs, I think you can assume that this will grow one in Q1. With the appraisal cycle, there will be a one-time kind of increase. And after that, we expect it to be kind of more or less stable for the rest of the year.

items.statement: Industry active clients plateaued at ~50M; growth driven by bull runs (10-15% long-term CAGR); next expansion depends on market cycle and FII inflows
items.quote: If you look at a longer frame the industry is growing like a 10% to 15% CAGR. On the questions on settlement I think that I remember now is basically it is on the customer demand...

items.statement: F&O penetration dropped to ~10% from ~18% pre-Nov'24; MTF, commodities, ETFs offset ARPU decline; MTF share of cash ADTO ~5-10%
items.quote: The penetration of F&O is still in like 10% around range, which used to be like 18 odd percent before November.

items.statement: Regulatory uncertainty on algo trading and F&O curbs; Groww waits for clarity before scaling algo; participates with regulators on investor protection
items.quote: We believe the new regulations that are still kind of getting cleaned up over a period of time will give us more clarity and we will probably jump into this market once we have full clarity on the regulatory piece.

items.statement: Wealth management (Fisdom, W, Prime) early stage; Fisdom target profitability by FY28; cross-sell exists but flows still being streamlined
items.quote: In the shareholder letter you have called out that Fisdom should be profitable by FY28.

items.statement: AI deployed across SDLC, customer support (GR1 co-pilot), operations; enables faster shipping with same headcount (~1,800); no plans to reduce engineering count
items.quote: So currently, how we think it is with the same strengths, Can we ship more? Can we ship faster and can we ship higher quality, right?

items.statement: Settlement cycle unchanged at quarterly (10 years); no regulator signal to shorten; instant withdrawal option available; not hitting single-script OI limits (<50% utilization)
items.quote: It has been quarterly since last 10 years now and I think it is again a choice. We haven't seen a customer being choosing bill to bill settlement significantly more than monthly or quarterly.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 1.5% to 3.5% YoY in constant currency
items.quote: Our revenue growth guidance for the financial year 2027 is 1.5% to 3.5% growth year -on-year in constant currency terms.

items.statement: FY27 operating margin guidance of 20% to 22%
items.quote: Our operating margin guidance for financial year '27 is 20% to 22%.

items.statement: Expect acceleration of growth in Financial Services and Energy, Utilities, Resources and Services verticals
items.quote: We expect acceleration of growth in F inancial Services and in E nergy, Utility, Resources and Services vertical.

items.statement: Full year large deal TCV of $14.9 bn, up 28% YoY; Q4 large deal TCV of $3.2 bn
items.quote: Large deals were very good, $14.9 bn for the full year, $3.2 bn for the fourth quarter. The full year was 28% higher than it was in the previous year.

items.statement: Net new component of large deals was 55% for the full year
items.quote: We see on the large deals, the net new is pretty large for the full year at 55%.

items.statement: FY26 operating margin at 21%; Q4 margin at 20.9%
items.quote: If you look at the margins, the full year margins is at 21%. The quarterly margins also 20.9%, very close to 21%.

items.statement: Q4 margin walk: -50 bps acquisition amortization, -30 bps one-off benefit reversal, -20 bps comp, +40 bps currency, +30 bps Maximus performance
items.quote: If you look at the puts and takes of the margin walk from the last quarter, we got 50 basis points impact from an acquisition-related amortization that we absorbed. There was a 30 basis points of one- off benefit that we got in Q3, so you know when you compare, that is a headwind. And 20 basis points was on account of comp-related matters. That was partially offset by 40 basis points of currency b

items.statement: FY27 margin headwinds include 60-70 bps from acquisition-related costs
items.quote: There is competitiveness in the market, there is acquisition that we have done. The acquisition related cost will impact margins by another 60 to 70 basis points.

items.statement: Hired over 20,000 freshers in FY26; plan to hire at least 20,000 freshers in FY27

items.statement: Headcount declined 8,000 sequentially in Q4 but grew 5,000 YoY for FY26
items.quote: So if you look at the headcount, our headcount sequentially has gone down by 8,000 employees but if you look at on a year -on-year basis it has still grown by 5,000.

items.statement: Wage hike quantum and timing not yet decided for FY27
items.quote: On the wage, we have not really made a decision at this point in time on the quantum and the timing of it. Once we decide we will let you know.

items.statement: AI services revenue growing nicely, higher than 5.5% of revenue reported in Q3, but exact number not disclosed
items.quote: No, it is growing. It is much more growth but we are not giving the number , but it is growing very nicely here.

items.statement: AI services across six areas (strategy engineering, data, process, legacy modernization, physical AI, trust) using Topaz Fabric and Cobalt platforms
items.quote: We see a large addressable market for AI services across the six areas that we mentioned - AI strategy engineering, data, process, legacy modernization, physical AI and trust. With our Topaz Fabric platform for AI and our Cobalt platform for cloud, we have differentiated capabilities that are operational today and that are working with our clients across each of these six areas of the AI landscape

items.statement: Strong growth in Financial Services, Communications, Manufacturing verticals and Europe geography in FY26
items.quote: We had strong growth in Financial Services, in Communications, in Manufacturing from the industry side and Europe on the geography side.

items.statement: Manufacturing vertical facing challenges, especially European auto; specific client wind-down baked into FY27 guidance
items.quote: Manufacturing per se is going through a challenging environment, especially the auto, in the European automobile sector. items.statement: Pricing environment stable; FY26 growth was pricing-led as volumes were softer; AI revenue coming at better pricing
items.quote: In terms of pricing, I think pricing environment for us has remained stable. On the contrary, actually, most of our growth this year has been pricing-led because the volumes have been softer. And that in a way corroborates with the fact that the AI revenue are coming at a better pricing.

items.statement: Continued competitive intensity and AI productivity impact factored into FY27 guidance
items.quote: As we look ahead to the financial year 2027, we see large opportunities in AI services. We also see continued competitive intensity and we see an AI productivity impact, a combination of these things.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions (Iran war) created economic uncertainty; seeing paths to stabilization and underlying resilience in Western economies
items.quote: Now with the situation with the Iran war, there was a change in the economic environment. Now from what we are seeing, there seems to be paths towards things stabilizing. We hope everyone sort of gets there. From then what we understand like, just talking to people in the market and the clients is that, the underlying resilience of some of the economies where we have the big markets is pretty good

items.statement: Board actively overseeing AI strategy; Nandan Nilekini deeply involved in Topaz Fabric vision
items.quote: The Board is very active in our AI work looking at it and actually Nandan himself is very active because he is got a very good vision on where the AI is going and also helping like a lot of the Topaz Fabric what we have done you know he is working to give us the ideas.

items.statement: Acquisition pipeline strong; focus on strategic, cultural, value fit in areas like healthcare and insurance
items.quote: will continue to do acquisitions. There is a good pipeline. items.statement: Visa costs remained stable; H1B visas not filed in new regime

items.statement: Over 90% of employees skilled on AI platforms; building forward deployed engineer teams for AI solutions
items.quote: So, both of those are getting developed quite rapidly and the skilling has gone on I think over 90% of our people -- yes about just over 90% of people are now getting skilled on different types of the AI platforms.

items.quote: Our revenue growth guidance of financial year '27 is 1.5% to 3.5% year-on-year in constant currency terms.

items.statement: FY27 effective tax rate expected 29% to 30%
items.quote: We expect effective tax rates for the FY27 to be in the range of 29% to 30%.

items.quote: Adjusted operating margin was stable at 21%. Gains from currency and Maximus were reinvested in talent, AI and sales and marketing.

items.statement: Onboarded 20,000+ freshers in FY26; expect similar hiring in FY27
items.quote: We onboarded more than 20,000 freshers in FY26 and expect to hire a similar number in FY27.

items.statement: DSO including unbilled net of unearned reduced to 78 days, lowest in seven years

items.quote: In line with our capital allocation policy, board has proposed a final dividend of INR25 per share which will result in a total dividend of INR48 per share, an increase of 11.6% over last year, once the final dividend is approved by the shareholders.

items.statement: FY26 growth led by realization increase from Project Maximus; volumes flattish

items.quote: if you look at Calendar '25, and just the 1st Quarter of the Calendar '26, effectively foreigners have pulled out $40 billion out of India. So, our international business honestly is just feeling the pain of that outflow front and center

items.statement: UTI market share: 5.5% of industry gross sales in Q4 FY26, 6.1% for full FY26
items.quote: UTI was able to capture a market share of 5.5% of the gross sales of the industry during this quarter and market share of 6.1% of the gross sales for the financial year FY26

items.statement: Expects consolidated EBITDA margin of 13.5-14% sustainable
items.quote: continue to assume that we will be able to maintain this EBITDA level 13.5% to 14% safely. Preet Pitani: Across continent? Sunil Chordia: on a consolidated basis

items.statement: Thailand volume growth 10-11% in FY27 to 55,000-56,000 tons due to capacity constraint
items.quote: Thailand we are not expecting 20%, we are expecting around 10% to 14% because there is a capacity constraint in Thailand. We are doing some debottlenecking, so Thailand from current year volume which is close to 51,000 will grow to 55,000 to 56,000.

items.statement: North America export growth target ~30%, Europe ~50%, Southeast Asia 10-15% in FY27
items.quote: we have a plan to grow around 30% in North Amer ica I can tell you. And some growth in Europe, which will be aroun d 50% and Southeast Asia 10%, 15% because we were supplies in South Asia for many, many years

items.statement: Chennai capacity doubling to 60,000 tons by Q2 FY27 with INR25 crore capex

items.statement: Chennai plant utilization 85-90% in Q4 FY26, expanding from 30,000 to 60,000 tons by Q2 FY27

That is why we decided to put in the money for balance equipment and some equipments have started arriving and we will become a 60,000 tons capacity plant by second quarter of this financial year.

items.statement: Indore and Thailand plants operating at ~90% utilization in FY26
items.quote: Indore continue to operate at 90% capacity utilization and so Thailand. Okay. So our capacity utilizations have been to peak level both in Thailand and Indore Pithampur.

items.quote: Particularly in this quarter, we could not achieve the EBITDA targeted EBITDA. That is because of the high prices of raw material. There was a sudden increase in steel prices beginning from January. So from January till March, the prices went up by almost INR10,000 a ton, which we could not pass on to the customer. That is why the EBITDA percentage in this quarter has gone down.

items.statement: Robust demand from all customers in India, Thailand and globally; no negative impact from geopolitics yet
items.quote: But we have been able to pass on the price increase in the current quarter and we see a robust demand from all our customers in India, as well as in Thailand and globally also.

items.statement: FY26 sales volume 133,000+ tons, up 18% YoY, highest ever

items.quote: And in tyre sector, our market share has again reached to 42% to 43%, which had come down to 35% to 37%.

items.statement: FY26 India exports ~9,000 tons; targeting ~15,000 tons in FY27
items.quote: Next year probably we are expecting to touch about 15,000 tons of export from India.

items.statement: US tariffs under Section 232 apply equally to all imports, no volume impact, tariff passed through US entity
items.quote: Tariffs have not affected the volume or the business because tariff we are under Section 232 where US has put tariff against all the imports , whether it is coming from India or Thailand or China or Mexico. So we are at par with all other countries. So it is not

items.quote: That has increased because of US export because the US export that happens, we first supply to our company in USA who imports, pays 50% duty on the product. So that amount also adds on to the working capital cost and then customer pays us in 30 or 60 days after he receives the material.

items.statement: Thailand avg 30 days receivables, India 50-60 days; exports longer due to 45-60 day shipping plus credit
items.quote: Thailand is overall average 30 days and India is about 50 to 60 days and then some working capital for stocking and finished good and raw material. But export has a longer working capital cycle because Europe shipping line takes 45 days to reach, USA takes anything from 45 to 60 days and then there is a credit to be extended.

items.statement: Working capital borrowing to continue at 7-7.5% cost; term loan to reduce by ~INR50 crore in FY27
items.quote: Long-term loan will be less than INR50 crores this year because repayment has to be done that much. Last year also we have reduced the long-term loan to that extent. And working capital might be required because of high prices now because there is a price increase of around 10% to 15% and also the increase in volume.

items.statement: Export mix: 70% tyre segment approvals, non-tyre growing faster due to quicker approvals
items.quote: I would say 70% of the efforts and development is happening in tyre segment in terms of number of counters and number of plants. But today, non-tyre segment volume is also substantial. But this ratio will keep changing because tyre companies take a long time to approve. Other products are faster approvals and volumes come in faster. So it's a mix of both.

items.statement: Industry growth estimated at 6-7% in FY26 vs FY25; company grew 14.8% to INR315.8 cr
items.quote: In what we estimate, as an industry that may register a growth of 6% to 7% versus FY25, your company registered a growth of 14.8% with INR315.8 crores revenue versus FY25 revenue of INR275.1 crores.

items.statement: Full-year PBT improved to INR16.99 cr from INR10.7 cr; material cost saving of 1% of revenue achieved
items.quote: Coming to the full year bottom line, your company significantly improved bottom line and delivered a PBT of INR 16.99 crores for FY26 versus INR10.7 crores in FY25.

items.quote: A couple of words on the bottom line of Q4 FY26, where the company registered a INR6.4 crores PBT versus INR9.4 crores last Q4.

items.quote: Specifically, in Q4 FY26, raw material prices suddenly shot up, riding on geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. And just to illustrate the magnitude, in February 2026, on average, the PE pipe grades saw a 58%, 59% price increase.

items.statement: Non-subsidy business contribution reached 35% in FY26 from 3% in FY20; projects ~25% of total revenue
items.quote: In fact, you will be happy to note that we reached a 35% contribution of non-subsidy business for FY26 from a mere 3% in FY20.

items.statement: Opening pipeline for irrigation projects at INR54 cr with potential upside of INR20 cr
items.quote: So this year we have an opening pipeline of about INR55 crores. And we see a further upside so that is very clear to us that INR55 crores and then we see a possible upside of another INR20 crores on top of that as we start the year.

items.statement: Receivables increased significantly; 80-90% from subsidy business; most acknowledged at final disbursement stages
items.quote: So I would say that about 80% to 90% of it comes from the subsidy business. So it is predominantly coming from our subsidy business.

items.statement: Capex plans for FY27 focused on productivity improvement and capacity expansion for current product lines with quick payback expectation
items.quote: Most of our capex plans are focused on improving productivity and on capacity expansion they're focused on current product lines, and we choose them carefully.

items.quote: As a result, the Industry Irrigation Association has also made a representation to the government requesting for a price increase, and the government may consider the industry's representation.

items.quote: But in the non-subsidy part, it is the farmer who will decide what is the right price. items.statement: No specific EBITDA margin outlook given; will use product mix, geography mix, and procurement timing to manage margins amid raw material volatility
items.quote: We don't tend to give outlooks. I mean as of now what we would say is that our approach will broadly follow the lines that I described. We don't have a control on what happens to raw material prices, but as an organization we will use the levers at our disposal to manage our business and deliver the best results we can in these circumstances.

items.statement: Employee cost increase due to contractual alignment for new labor code (Code on Social Security 2020), not hiring or variable pay
items.quote: It is largely attributed to the labor code, the new labor code. So it's largely attributable to the contractual alignment of the employee benefits in anticipation of the wage code.

items.statement: Government target of 2 million hectares annually (10 million over 5 years) vs 1 million hectares in FY25; central fund release accelerated with 43% issued by May 2025

items.statement: Raw material price volatility seen as key risk for Q1 FY27; geopolitical events difficult to predict
items.quote: The only caveat here is that geopolitical events are difficult to predict and hence, we see reason to be cautious on this front for Q1 FY27.

items.quote: Yes, so we are we welcome them and their representation on the board. They come as people with deep industry experience, and they will definitely add value to our discussions and our approach going forward.

items.statement: Distributed manufacturing with satellite units improving asset utilization and freight/processing cost control

items.statement: Negative free cash flow over 3-5 years due to receivables build-up; strategy to balance revenue streams for better cash conversion
items.quote: The pressure on cash flows, as you know, in this industry is almost entirely due to receivables. And while we have managed our working capital very actively through tighter inventory control, receivable build-up has tended to happen in a few key states where the margins are good.

items.statement: Industry restructuring toward cash-and-carry models; company shifting from EPC dependence to non-subsidy products
items.quote: Leading firms are shifting focus towards cash and carry models, reducing dependence on EPC projects with long payment cycles and expanding into non-subsidy-based products to improve their liquidity, which exactly is what your company is doing.

items.statement: GST reduction from 12% to 5% expected to have positive demand impact in medium to long term
items.quote: We also think that the recent GST changes, such as the reduction of GST from 12% to 5%, is likely to have a positive demand impact in the medium term to the long term.

items.statement: Micro irrigation penetration at 17-18% of 72 million hectare potential; potential doubles if surface water included
items.quote: As we look at the potential and the existing penetration of micro irrigation in India, we see only about 17% to 18% penetration of the total identified current potential for micro irrigation, which is 72 million hectares.

items.statement: Aspiring for mid- to high single-digit organic growth year-over-year in FY27
items.quote: we are aspiring for mid - to high single -digit organic growth year -over-year. There are, of course, dynamics at play in the market, but we feel confident that two-three of our markets will produce enough strength to get us there.

I also want to reiterate that the Board has asked us to continue to stick with the 40% to 50% pay out, which is what has been given back to shareholders every year, and this will now happen not just through dividend, but through the right combination of dividend and buyback.

items.statement: Addressable market opportunity of INR 14,000-15,000 crore across Gujarat, Rajasthan, Maharashtra, Uttarakhand, Odisha, Jharkhand, and railway electrification.
items.quote: Addressable market in the coming future, we are seeing roughly around INR 14,000 crore to INR 15,000 crore.

items.statement: Expanding transmission footprint pan-India (Maharashtra, Odisha, Jharkhand); non-Gujarat order book share to move from 10-15% to 20% near term.
items.quote: We are looking at very aggressive bidding for projects outside Gujarat. So eventually this number will start moving towards 80%-20%, in the near term.

items.statement: IKS signed definitive merger agreement to acquire TruBridge for $557M enterprise value ($427M equity + $130M debt)
items.quote: IKS is buying TruBridge, which is listed on the NASDAQ, for an overall enterprise value of $557 million, which is about $427 million in equity value and then we inherit their debt of about $130 million.

items.statement: Total debt will be under $600M at close, 5-year term at SOFR+275bps stepping down to SOFR+175bps, starting leverage ~3x EBITDA
items.quote: That will lead to a total debt of a little under $600 million for IKS at the time of closing, which we have secured for a 5-year term on a fairly decent interest rate of a SOFR plus 275 bps, which eventually slides down to SOFR plus 175 bps as our leverage ratio keeps coming down.

items.statement: Deal expected to be PAT and EPS accretive instantly at close, pre-synergies
items.quote: The deal is, like I was saying, expected to be PAT and EPS accretive instantly at close.

items.statement: Combined trailing 12-month revenue ~$698M, adjusted EBITDA ~$186M at close (IKS $117M + TruBridge $69M adjusted)
items.quote: The combined business, if you take trailing 12 months calendar 25, would be about $698 million in revenue and $159 million in EBITDA, but really $186 million in EBITDA when you adjust out a couple of items from TruBridge's $43 million EBITDA $9.5 million in ESOP costs which will obviously go away.

items.statement: TruBridge has 700+ hospitals (0-50 beds) driving $32B revenue, 40%+ market share in segment, 30% overall rural hospital market share
items.quote: TruBridge focuses on the small segment of these hospitals, which is the 0 to 50 beds. Typically, these rural community hospitals tend to be about 0 to 200 beds. TruBridge focuses on the 0 to 50 beds, and by number of hospital count, they have about 700 hospitals, which is maybe 40% plus market share in the 0 to 50 beds and overall 30% market share over the 2,200 beds.

items.statement: Rural hospital market: 2,200 hospitals, $164B revenue, 60M+ patients (20% of US population), 60-70% outpatient care similar to IKS physician base
items.quote: Just to put it in perspective, there are 2,200 rural hospitals in America that drive $164 billion of revenue. So even as I'm calling it a niche market segment, it's a very large market segment. 20% of America lives in this rural setting, so you're talking about 60 million plus patients driving $164 billion of revenue across 2,200-odd hospitals.

items.statement: TruBridge RCM business $220M revenue with ~3,500 FTEs globally; IKS tech-led model achieves higher revenue per FTE
items.quote: You know, it's about a $220 million business and they do that business using, give or take, 3,500 FTEs globally, right? Which is a whole different, if we want to put a revenue per FTE metric, it's a whole different revenue per FTE metric than the revenue per FTE metric that one is able to deliver in our technology-led platform system of action in the RCM part of it.

items.statement: TruBridge revenue split: $126M EHR (system of record) + $221M RCM (partial system of action); IKS has 16-18 task platform system of action
items.quote: Trailing 12 months 2025 calendar year, which is also their fiscal year, $347 million in revenue, about $126 million of that comes from the EHR business and about $221 million comes from the RCM business.

items.statement: Immediate cross-sell opportunity: $450M white space in TruBridge's 700-hospital install base for RCM at conservative 2% take rate (vs current ~3%)
items.quote: And taking that sort of 2% odd take rate, that creates a $660 million immediately addressable TAM. And TruBridge's RCM revenue is around $220 million, so it creates about $450 million of white space in their captive install base.

items.statement: TruBridge adjusted EBITDA $69M (FY25) after removing $9.5M ESOP costs and non-recurring public company/consulting expenses
items.quote: Doing all that, they've been delivering an adjusted EBITDA of about $69 million in fiscal 25 and obviously the opportunity to continue to grow that.

items.statement: RCM take rates modeled at conservative 2% vs current ~3% due to expected price compression from agentic AI automation
items.quote: We're taking a take rate of 2%. Why are we taking two percent? because today's take rates, by the way, in their business are even higher, they're closer to 3%. But we're modeling it at 2% because we believe that as we ourselves build agentic AI-based orchestration of tasks that can be orchestrated autonomously or even with some human in the loop, there will be some price compression.

items.statement: Integration will enable real-time native workflow orchestration (vs async API), transforming tools like ambient scribing from post-visit to clinical co-pilot and enabling denial prediction at point of care
items.quote: Now instead of it being a post-visit tool, now it can truly function like a clinical co-pilot where during the live encounter it is servicing diagnosis for the doctor, suggesting diagnosis based on the conversation. It's actually servicing care gaps that they need to plug, documentation that they need to plug in order to be able to bill in the most comprehensive compliant manner as possible.

items.statement: Starting leverage ~3x EBITDA higher than preferred, but comfortable due to instant EPS accretion, 5x interest coverage, and rapid deleveraging via internal accruals
items.quote: And this puts our starting leverage at a little over 3x EBITDA, which traditionally speaking I would say is a bit more than I'd genuinely like. But I think given the strategic rationale and the rapid pace at which we think we can deleverage through internal accruals given that the deal is instantly EPS accretive at close and there is a whole bunch of opportunity to drive both synergies and growth

items.statement: Transaction expected to close in 3-4 months; TruBridge net debt of $130M at March 31 will likely decrease as cash-flow generative business
items.quote: And so given that it's probably going to take somewhere between three to four months to close this transaction, that $130 million, given that they're a cash flow generating business, that $130 million of debt will come down, which will then take down our total debt or possibly the debt attributable to this deal and the interest cost associated with it.

items.statement: Management sets a 4-year True North target of INR 3,000 crores EBITDA by end of FY30, up from INR 1,000 crores trailing 12 months Dec 2025, with net debt returning to Dec 2025 levels (~INR 300 crores).
items.quote: we feel comfortable to say that we should be, in my -- and please, I want to caveat this again and again, this is not a guidance, and I know that even if I say that you guys will assume whatever it is, but this is our true north. This is the financial manifest of all the execution that I talked about, all the vectors of growth, all the vectors of the strategic transformation of the EHR, creation o

items.statement: Signed agreement to acquire TruBridge; expected to close in 90-120 days pending HSR approval from FTC, followed by 4-5 quarter integration.
items.quote: we signed the agreement yesterday. It's expected to take 90 to 120 days to close. In that timeframe, we absolutely operate like totally independent companies, focus on our individual objectives, work through the regulatory approval process, which includes the HSR approval from the FTC, which is the Federal Trade Commission. Once the transaction closes, we anticipate a 4 to 5-year, four to five qua

items.statement: TruBridge has 700 rural hospital EHR clients (0-50 beds) with $32B revenue flowing through them; RCM revenue is $220M on a $660M addressable TAM in installed base, implying $450M white space.
items.quote: TruBridge's RCM revenue is around $220 million, so it creates about $450 million of white space in their captive install base.

items.statement: Total rural hospital RCM market is $3.5B; outsourced portion is ~$1B growing at 12-13%, with 30% penetration currently.
items.quote: Even if you take out the TruBridge install base of $660 million, you're still talking about a $3 billion hospital market on which there is about 30% penetration. So there's a $1 billion outsourced rural hospital market, and that's growing at 12% to 13%.

items.statement: TruBridge RCM stack covers front, middle, back office with proprietary tech including Get Real Health patient engagement, proprietary clearinghouse, and TruCode encoder SaaS ($650M TAM).
items.quote: the potential market in which one can sell the TruCode tool actually itself is about $650 million TAM, and so one of our endeavors will be to accelerate that sales motion.

items.statement: IKS has 17,000+ employees including 2,000 clinically trained and 800+ technologists to accelerate EHR modernization and platform integration.
items.quote: we have a pretty large, further scalable efficient operating platform with 17,000-plus people, of which 2,000 are clinically trained, 800-plus technologists.

items.statement: TruBridge has 3,000 RCM FTEs (1,000+ in US) with largely US-centric delivery; IKS's optimized offshore-enabled model expected to create operating and G&A synergies.
items.quote: they still have a very largely US-centric RCM delivery model. Remember they have 2,000-plus RCM FTEs between actually 3,000 RCM FTEs between US and India already of which 1,000-plus are in the US. So, obviously that creates both operating and G&A synergies.

items.statement: Rural EHR market is a two-player market (TruBridge 40% share in 0-50 beds, MEDITECH) with Oracle Cerner as challenger; MEDITECH lacks RCM offering, Oracle exited RCM; pure-play BPO competitors are Med-Metrix and CorroHealth.
items.quote: the rural hospital market is already a mature market and nearly already mature enough to be just a two-player market between TruBridge and MEDITECH, with Oracle trying to be the challenger to the two main incumbents, which are MEDITECH and TruBridge.

items.statement: TruCode encoder competes with 3M and Optum but is gaining share as a challenger; autonomous coding unlikely due to deterministic nature of coding vs non-deterministic GenAI.
items.quote: we've seen TruBridge take market share in a small way from 3M and Optum, which are the dominant players in this space.

items.statement: IKS will deploy Scribble ambient clinical documentation suite and AI-first patient engagement (patent-pending) into TruBridge install base; TruBridge currently partners with Microsoft DAX for ambient documentation.
items.quote: if this transaction closes as you can imagine we would manifest our entire Scribble suite in their entire install base and because of their EHR incumbency, their take on that is just a no-brainer, I mean the customers are dying for it.

items.statement: Historical 10-year IKS trajectory: 28% revenue CAGR and 33% EBITDA CAGR; AQuity acquisition pro forma EBITDA improved from 24% to early/mid-30s in ~5 quarters.
items.quote: Look at our 10-year trajectory at IKS, we've actually delivered 28% revenue growth and 33% EBITDA CAGR.

items.statement: Launching build of acute RCM small language model (SLM) on proprietary data to reduce compute cost and create self-learning loop; will expand SLMs to other platform tasks over time.
items.quote: we're actually launching the start of building a small language model. We'll start with an acute RCM small language model. Now why a small language model? Small language model has two benefits, right? It starts to build its own -- it's built out of its own proprietary data, and over a period of time it reduces the cost of compute, right?

items.statement: Cross-sell of RCM into TruBridge EHR installed base (700 hospitals, 30% RCM penetration) is immediate low-hanging fruit; buyers for EHR and RCM are same (CEO/CFO), enabling faster cross-sell vs AQuity experience.
items.quote: the buyer of the electronic health record is the same as the buyer of the revenue cycle. The buyer of the electronic health record is the CEO, the CFO, and the CMO. The buyer of the revenue cycle is the CEO, CFO. And so we're not going to now cross-sell a new service into a different part of their organization, and that creates a whole different type of immediacy in the opportunity that it creates

items.statement: Management acknowledges short-term learnings, surprises, and potential mistakes during integration; 4-year True North factors in uncertainty but avoids quantifying synergy breakdown.
items.quote: it is a strategic transformative acquisition. It will have short-term learnings, surprises. I can tell you that if you look at my track record and our company's track record and our management's track record as a public company over the last five quarters that we've declared. As a company even before we went public, we try to be in the space where we like to under-promise and over-deliver.

items.statement: TruBridge EHR processes $32B of hospital revenue across 700 hospitals; RCM take rate modeled at 2% (conservative vs 3% potential) due to expected price compression from agentic AI orchestration.
items.quote: taking that sort of 2% odd take rate, that creates a $660 million immediately addressable TAM.

items.statement: Transaction requires HSR approval from US Federal Trade Commission (FTC) as part of regulatory closure process.
items.quote: work through the regulatory approval process, which includes the HSR approval from the FTC, which is the Federal Trade Commission.

items.statement: Same-store sales growth of 34% in Q4 FY26 demonstrates resilient consumer demand across all three months.
items.quote: Same-store sales growth of 34% this quarter demonstrates that demand environment is resilient. Growth was broad-based, with homogeneous SSG growth trends across all three months of the quarter.

items.statement: Operated 340 stores across 134 cities as of March 2026, adding 17 stores in Q4 and 65 stores for the full year FY26.
items.quote: As of March '26, we operated 340 stores across 134 cities, adding 17 stores during the quarter and 65 stores for the year, significantly strengthening our national footprint.

items.statement: Targeting approximately 20% annual store growth on the total base of 340 stores for FY27 and beyond.
items.quote: So I think generally what we have maintained or what we are trying to maintain for last one to two years is adding close to 20% to our distribution on an annual basis.

items.statement: Pre-IndAS EBITDA margin improved substantially YoY in FY26 despite studded mix shift, demonstrating operating leverage.
items.quote: if you look at YoY, there has been a substantial improvement in the margin at the pre - Ind AS level. Second is this improvement is despite the shift in mix, which kind of demonstrates that as the growth accelerates, as we build more presence across categories and drive more wallet share with our existing customers, there is still a fair amount of operatin g leverage which is ahead of us in the bu

items.statement: Vertically integrated model enables sweating gold effectively and using alternate materials to restore price accessibility without compromising design.
items.quote: Our rapid realignment of entry - level offerings leveraging our vertically integrated model enabled us to restore price accessibility without compromising design or experience. The benefit of this recalibration are clearly visible in Q4 and are expected to c ontinue through FY27

items.statement: Studded revenue contribution exited FY26 close to 60%, down from ~68% in FY25 due to gold price surge; management views plain gold and studded as additive, not substitutive.
items.quote: See, I think we can come back with that exact number, but again as I said, the exit it will be close to 60%, but at the exit rates and variances obviously are there on a quarter-on-quarter basis, right?

items.statement: Inventory turns declined to 1.13x in FY26 from 1.34x in FY25, primarily due to sharp gold price increase inflating closing inventory value; mature stores achieve 1.7-1.9x turns.
items.quote: So I think this year one of the most, one of the kind of one-offs that happened in this financial year was the sharp increase in gold, which has actually led to a very sharp increase in the value of closing inventory. Okay, so this is a one-off and this is the case with almost all the players in the industry where the closing inventory is kind of disproportionately higher than the sale numbers for

items.statement: Franchisee stores (67 of 340) will see substantial drop in FY27-FY28 as five-year contracts expire; not accelerating exits for relationship reasons.
items.quote: From a trendline perspective, I think ‘ 27 and ‘2 8 should see a significant drop in terms of this classical franchisee model that we have had historically. So ‘27 and ‘28 is going to see a substantial drop in terms of the franchisee - owned company - operated stores

items.statement: ESOP charge of INR 93 crore in FY26 (front-loaded accounting), dropping to INR 58 crore then INR 28 crore; 90% held by top 6 management; 1.7% unallocated pool sufficient for 3-4 years.
items.quote: And hence when we see almost INR 93 crores of that charge came in the first year itself, but then it's dropping down to INR 58 crores and then INR 28 crores and then bottoming out. And essentially, going forward also, we don't see ourselves deviating much from this plan. Beyond this, we have around 1.7% of unallocated ESOP pool on a fully diluted basis and we don't foresee ourselves breaching that

items.statement: Mature stores (3-4+ years vintage) achieve revenue run-rate of INR 14-15 crore per store at minimum with pre-IndAS EBITDA margins of ~23.8% (excluding inventory gains).
items.quote: It doesn't include any inventory gain.

items.statement: Store size rationale: larger stores (~2,000 sq ft) avoid costly relocations as rental delta vs small stores is minimal; vertically integrated model carries manufacturing inventory on balance sheet.
items.quote: Now the cost of that relocation is actually pretty high and the rental delta between let's say opening a 1,200 square feet store and 2,000 square feet store generally is not that high because on a high street or in a mall when you actually try to look for a smaller store, it's not that the rental is not proportional.

items.statement: Launched industry-first exclusive men's and kids' jewellery stores to expand demographic reach and wallet share; repeat customers contributing meaningfully.
items.quote: I think at this point it would be relevant for me to highlight one of the new initiatives that we have undertaken, is probably industry’s unique and first kind of its own experiment as we set up an exclusive store that focused on offering men’s and kids’ j ewellery to our consumers

items.statement: Gold price volatility creates near-term ROIC pressure via inventory MTM; long-term ROIC normalizes over 5-10 year cycles; franchisee capital structure available as lever if gold CAGR sustains.
items.quote: Now if you believe that that is how gold will continue to behave over the longer term, then I think what you’re asking is a fair question. But I think if you look at broadly these normalized gold price movements over several years, you can take 5 - 10 year b locks, then I think obviously all this kind of short - term volatility etc. kind of normalizes and thus I think long - term ROIC of the busin

items.statement: A&P spend stabilized at 6% of revenue (down from 12%); will grow in absolute terms while maintaining 6% ratio, shifting from performance marketing to brand building.
items.quote: In terms of numbers, our plan is to not drop it at below 6%. So I think over last two to three years we have come down from 12% to 6%, while in absolute terms it has grown up marginally, but the revenues outpaced it. So in percentage terms it has dropped from 12% to 6%. Now we are comfortable at that 6% level and as we move forward, we will increase it in absolute terms while keeping it static in

items.statement: Standalone revenue grew 49.1% YoY in Q4 FY26; full year FY26 revenue INR 2,441 crore recorded on retail sales basis including franchisee stores.
items.quote: For the quarter, standalone re venue grew 49.1% year - on - year and we delivered revenues of INR 2,441 crore s for the full year

items.statement: FY28 AUM growth guidance of 23-25% CAGR from FY25 base reaffirmed
items.quote: we had given a guidance for FY '28 where we had stated that over the period of FY '25 to FY '28, we will grow at 23% to 25%. So we are on track and working towards the same.

items.statement: FY26 PAT growth excluding non-recurring items at 36%, exceeding 32-35% guidance
items.quote: For the full year FY26, profit after tax excluding non-recurring items grew 36%, exceeding our guidance of 32% to 35%.

items.statement: FY26 cost-to-income ratio at 38.3%, within guided 38-39% range
items.quote: For FY26, the cost to income ratio stood at 38.3%, representing an improvement of 335 basis points over FY25 and remaining comfortably within our guided range of 38% to 39%.

items.statement: Consolidated AUM at INR2.77 lakh crore, up 20% YoY and 6% QoQ
items.quote: Our assets under management stood at INR2.77 lakh crores, up 20% year-on-year and up 6% sequentially.

items.statement: AUM excluding Motor Finance at INR2.52 lakh crore, up 28% YoY and 8% QoQ
items.quote: Excluding motor finance business, our AUM stood at INR2.52 lakh crores, growing 28% year - on-year and 8% sequentially, driven by sustained mom entum across our core segments

items.statement: Housing finance AUM grew 29% YoY to INR86,653 crore
items.quote: Our AUM grew 29% year-on-year to INR86,653 crores, while profit after tax increased 34% year-on-year reflecting both scale expansion and sustained earnings quality.

items.statement: Motor Finance AUM at INR25,390 crore, down 4% QoQ due to fitness-first approach
items.quote: The AUM stood at INR25,390 crores, a sequential decline of 4% reflecting our fitness-first approach.

items.statement: Q4 disbursements crossed INR50,000 crore for first time, up 32% YoY and 12% QoQ
items.quote: Quarter four set a new benchmark with disbursements crossing INR50,000 crores, a first for the company and a testament to our growing scale. Year-on-year, quarter four disbursements grew 32% and were 12% higher sequentially.

items.statement: Unsecured retail at 10.3% of AUM, targeting 15%
items.quote: With unsecured retail currently at 10.3% of AUM, we continue to see significant headroom towards our target of scaling this to 15% and we remain firmly on track to achieve this.

items.statement: Motor Finance non-Tata OEM share in new CV disbursements reached 26% in Q4
items.quote: our non-Tata OEM share in new commercial vehicle disbursements for quarter 4 has reached 26%, reflecting early success in our multi-OEM strategy.

items.statement: Net total income stable at 6.5% in Q4; expect NIM improvement in FY27 driven by high-yield product mix shift
items.quote: We continue to operate with stable margin corridor with Net total income in quarter 4 at 6.5%. Yields have remained healthy supported by disciplined pricing and a calibrated shift towards higher yielding segments.

items.statement: Consolidated net NPA down 10 bps QoQ to 0.9%; credit cost improved 30 bps QoQ to 0.9%
items.quote: Including the motor finance business, our gross stage 3 assets were 2% compared to 2.2% in the previous quarter, net stage 3 at 0.9%, and provision coverage ratio at 56.2%, all showing quarter-on-quarter improvement. Credit costs improved by ~30 basis points to 0.9% during the quarter.

items.statement: Ex-Motor Finance net NPA at 0.5%, credit cost at 0.8% in Q4
items.quote: Excluding the motor finance business, gross stage 3 assets continue to remain strong at 1.5%, net stage 3 at 0.5%, and provision coverage ratio at 65.1%. Credit cost declined to 0.8% for the quarter, reflecting a ~20 basis points improvement over quarter three.

items.statement: Housing finance credit cost stable at 0.1%, net NPA at 0.3%
items.quote: Asset quality continues to be our core strength. Credit costs remain stable at 0.1%, while net NPA stood at 0.3%, positioning us amongst the best performing players in the housing finance sector.

items.statement: Corporate lending ~14% of AUM; used opportunistically for high-rated names
items.quote: We did see an opportunity in the corporate business of looking at very high credit rated companies and we did use that opportunity. But on an overall basis, 86% is retail and SME.

items.statement: Motor Finance shifting mix: increasing used CV and small/mid CV, reducing heavy CV concentration
items.quote: We are increasing exposure to used commercial vehicles and small and mid-commercial vehicles while reducing our heavy commercial vehicle concentration.

items.statement: ROA improved 20 bps QoQ to 2.3% consolidated; 2.5% ex-Motor Finance; Housing Finance ROA at 2.6% in Q4
items.quote: Return on assets improved by ~20 basis points quarter-on-quarter to 2.3% and ROE improved by ~80 basis points from quarter three to 13.9% in quarter four of FY26.

items.statement: Motor Finance targeting ROA of 2% by FY28; expect steady improvement through FY27
items.quote: We expect steady ROA improvement through FY27 and we are targeting to reach an ROA of 2% by FY28 as we had communicated before.

items.statement: Housing Finance cost-to-income improved 320 bps YoY to 31.1% in FY26; below 30% in Q4
items.quote: Our focus on automation, Gen AI, and tighter operational control has resulted in improvement of cost to income ratio by ~320 basis points from 34.3% in FY25 to 31.1% in FY26. In fact, this cost to income dropped below 30% in quarter 4 of FY26.

items.statement: AI Underwriting Assist reduced SME credit memo prep from 2 days to 20 minutes; 30% productivity gain; 85% adoption
items.quote: Our underwriting assist platform, amongst the first in the industry, has reduced credit memo preparation time from 2 days to 20 minutes in our SME business, thereby improving productivity of the underwriting team by 30%. The adoption rate of underwriting assist platform today stands at 85%.

items.statement: AI Voice Hub: 90% welcome calls automated; AI-driven early bucket collections delivering 30% EMI collection of allocated pool
items.quote: Our unified voice hub operates across sales, service, and collections in 11 languages. 90% of welcome calls are automated and AI-driven early bucket calling is delivering 30% EMI collection of the allocated pool.

items.statement: No material stress observed from West Asia conflict; monitoring MSME working capital cycles weekly; portfolio diversified and granular
items.quote: As far as risk from geo-political environment is concerned, we have not observed any material stress in our portfolio across commercial vehicle as well as MSME segments. That said, we continue to monitor the developments closely, virtually spending time on this on a weekly basis to see where things are progressing.

items.statement: Caution exercised in select MSME segments regarding working capital cycle and raw material availability
items.quote: In terms of our assessment, we feel that we should be more careful in certain parts of the MSME business and this is where our messaging to our credit team is that you should look at some segments within the MSME and try to understand more, more from the working capital cycle at this point of time and availability of raw material.

items.statement: FY28 ROA guided at 2.5%-2.7%
items.quote: for FY28, we have guided for an ROA band of 2.5% to 2.7%.

items.statement: FY28 cost-to-income guided at 33%-34%
items.quote: we have said that cost to income should be between 33 to 34% and we do believe that is achievable.

items.statement: FY27 loan growth guided at 23%-25%
items.quote: given the fact that you're looking at around 23 % to 25% loan growth next year

items.statement: FY27 credit cost guided around 1%
items.quote: we do believe that the right credit cost for us would be some 1% and which is the guidance which we have given.

items.statement: FY27 cost of funds expected lower than FY26
items.quote: you had shared and guided that FY27 you expect your cost of funds to be lower than in FY26.

items.statement: NIM plus fee improved to 7.6% in affordable housing
items.quote: our NIM plus fee, which was in the region of 6.7, has improved to 7.6 in this financial year.

items.statement: Daily average yield fall lower than cost of funds fall
items.quote: on a daily average, we are seeing that the drop in yields is not more than the drop in cost of funds.

items.statement: Corporate lending yields 11%-13% with ROA 2.5%+
items.quote: In corporates, the yield may be more closer to maybe 11%, in developer it may be more closer to 12 %-13%. But more important, their return on assets is very good. They are all sort of 2.5 and above.

items.statement: Clean energy, developer finance, top corporates driving corporate loan growth

items.statement: Prime home loan and LAP growing at 21%+, micro housing >50%, affordable housing ~25%
items.quote: Our prime home loan and LAP is growing at 21% plus. Our micro housing is growing at over 50% and our affordable housing is growing at close to about 25%.

items.statement: Motor finance volumes growing for last 6-8 months after de-growth phase
items.quote: if you look at from the last April -May, we have only been growing now. So what dealers are seeing is that the phase of the volumes going down , the monthly volumes going down is over. Now for the last 6-8 months, they are only seeing incremental increase in volumes.

items.statement: Housing credit cost 10 bps in FY26, expected to continue
items.quote: our credit costs for the year have been 10 basis points and in fact if I look at the trends, I see no reason why things should be any different going forward.

items.statement: Retail unsecured credit costs improved QoQ from Q1 to Q4 FY26
items.quote: we started seeing a lowering of credit costs happening from Q2. Quarter two was lower than Q1, Q3 was lower than Q2 and Q4 was lower than Q3.

items.statement: Motor finance Q4 better than Q3, early indicators show no significant impact
items.quote: quarter 3 was good, but quarter 4 was even better for motor finance business. Though in motor finance I would only say it's we need to watch for quarter 1 and quarter 2 because quarter 3, quarter 4 usually are better. But looking at our early indicators of the quality of book we've created, we do not foresee any significant impact.

items.statement: April bounce rates lower than Q4 FY26
items.quote: actually we've seen a bounce rate coming down in April compared to quarter 4 of last year.

items.statement: No SME stress from war; raw material cost increases being passed on

items.statement: Enhanced due diligence on IT sector salaried borrowers for 12-18 months
items.quote: This is something which has been spoken about for the last, I would say, 12 to 18 months. And right from that stage, we had put some enhanced due diligence for this segment and we have been following that.

items.statement: FY27 branch network expansion of 10%-15%
