items.statement: Hot lead pipeline of close to $200 million with offers in market being sanitized and validated
items.quote: I would rather shed light on the hot lead pipeline, right? Because we're currently dealing with close to, I would say, 200 million odd USD with offers in the market, right?

items.statement: Current pipeline of ₹900 crore intended to be delivered in next 18 to 24 months
items.quote: So, as we said, that 900 crores are the current pipeline, which we will intend, which we will deliver in next 18 to 24 months.

items.statement: Contribution margins at 43.8% vs 45.9% previous year; pressure from Africa projects and portfolio mix
items.quote: If we see at a non-contribution margins, they are at 43.8, they are s till healthy compared to previous year, which was around 45.9%.

items.statement: Target contribution margin ~45%, EBITDA margin 13-14%, PAT margin 9-11% internally
items.quote: At operating level, we continue to, you know, operating as in contribution margins, we will ideally do around 45%, and at EBITDA level, our target is to do around 13 to 14%, and PAT level will be between 9 to 11% is what our internal targets are.

items.statement: Three main factors impacted margins: capability enhancement (talent acquisition), RMC cost up ~33%, execution cost up ~43% due to remobilization
items.quote: One was capability enhancement, which focuses on talent acquisition. One was the RMC cost, which grew up by close to 33%, and the last was the execution cost, which was up to 43%, which increased due to the remobilization of the installation t eam amidst the geographical conditions

items.statement: Freight cost increases compensated by dollar-denominated revenue; RMC procured in India so main challenge is freight
items.quote: If you look at main RMC cost, we still procure it in India, so I think the challenges is more on the freight piece, so delivery and execution can get delayed, but the impact on cost could be very small, you know, which will get compensated with. We're rising dollar because most of the revenue is in dollar terms.

items.statement: Receivables risen to ₹204.34 crore; receivable management now strategic priority with sharper collection-led discipline
items.quote: However, our focus for the next four quarters remains firmly centred on cash and collection , while our liquidity position remains strong. The receivables have risen to ₹ 204.34 crore. Accordingly, receivable management is now a strategic operational priority with sharper collection-led discipline being implemented to ensure that scale is supported by strong cash conversion and healthier working c

items.statement: Dubai receivables ₹37 crore, Saudi receivables ₹61 crore; high due to Q4 heavy billing, expected to reduce in Q1-Q2
items.quote: Our Receivables in Dubai is 37 crores, whereas in Saudi it is around 61 crores. This is part in, you know, typically because of last heavy quarter billing.

items.statement: GCC localization through subsidiaries: 100% subsidiary in UAE (FTS), 100% in Saudi (Fabtech Saudi), JV in Saudi (Mark Maker 33.33%), investment in TSA (16%), FABL (49%)
items.quote: We have 100% subsidiary called FTS in UAE, 100% subsidiary in Saudi Arabia called Fabtech Saudi, we have 33.33% in Mark Maker, which becomes our process OSD, closed loop line division, our own in-house investment of 16% now in TSA, which allows us to offer water systems across all the pharmaceutical projects, and FABL with 49%, which allows us to be a approved vendor for Containment solutions.

items.statement: Bidding for pre-engineered buildings and civil infrastructure to control project timelines, reduce greenfield execution from 24-27 months by ~20%
items.quote: Where we used to be at 24 to 27 months per greenfield project, now we're able to reduce that by, let's say, 20%.

items.statement: Expansion in Kenya showing extraordinary momentum; Africa emerging as powerful long-term growth corridor
items.quote: At the same time, our expansion in Kenya has demonstrated extraordinarily momentum, reinforcing our belief that Africa can emerge as a powerful long-term strategy corridor for Fabtech.

items.statement: Animal health segment growing in Middle East, North Africa, Saudi; secured vaccine fill-finish facility and multiple medical device/formulation projects in veterinary sector
items.quote: The animal health segment in medical devices in veterinary fields of vaccines and general formulations has been growing across the region. And we were able to bag not one but multiple projects in the Middle East, North African and Saudi Arabian region, which allowed us to secure a vaccine fill finish facility and multiple medical device and finish formulation projects in the veterinary sector.

items.statement: No cancellation risk in current geopolitical environment; clients have positive cash flows and understand pharmaceutical independence need
items.quote: Fortunately enough, this situation has not arose yet, and we don't expect it to, because even clients and the nations understand that pharmaceutical independence is needed for situations like this.

items.statement: Billing currency always USD via LCs; may move to Euros depending on war situation; never local currency due to devaluation risk
items.quote: No, it's LC back payment terms always, and it's always in USD currently, which we are currently having discussions with our finance teams and leaders in the market and th e board. We may move to Euros depending on the situation with the war, obviously. But never in local currency, because, as you know, pharmaceutical emerging markets that we operate in, currencies can get devalued, dollar remains

items.statement: Order conversion rate improved to 11% and reaching 16-17% of hot leads; expect huge order booking in coming quarters
items.quote: In nutshell, looking at our conviction and commitment in last quarter, you know, in that disruptive environment, we can say that our conversion is now getting improved. It is now 11% and it is reaching and hitting to around 16 to 17 percent of the hot lead.

items.statement: Leadership transition to Executive Chairman structure for sharper strategy direction, governance alignment, and long-term oversight; management continues execution
items.quote: The transition to executive chairman should not be viewed as a return to the operation, but rather as a move towards sharper strategy direction, strong governance alignment, and bolder long -term oversight. Simply put, management will continue to drive execution, while the executive chairman structure will help ensure that Fabtech remains strategically aligned towards th e right market, right oppo

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions disrupted supply chains, impacted freight economics, introduced volatility; pressure on profitability during critical execution phase of last quarter
items.quote: This year, however, came with extraordinary challenges. Global geopolitical tensions and the regional conflicts disrupted supply chains, impacted freight economics, and introduced volatility across the key markets. These factors did exert pressure on profitability, particularly during the critical execution phase of the last quarter.

items.statement: Other income more than doubled to ₹21 crore: major component ₹12 crore forex income, ₹7 crore interest on FDs from IPO funds and lending facilities
items.quote: other income, the major component of 20 crores is around 12 crores of foreign income. Forex. So different exchange rate and the balance amount, 7 crores are from the interest fund on the FDs which we have parked from the IPO fund and the oth er FDs for our lending facilities

items.statement: Strategic market penetration in cost-effective markets like Africa increases volume but lowers margins; volume increase will balance margins in near future
items.quote: There were active strategi c calls that Fabtech has taken to focus on a market penetration strategy in cost-effective markets such as Africa as well. And we would be fair to say that this strategy has allowed us to win more projects and increase the order pipeline, also focus on internal margin development, which you will see in the quarters to come

items.statement: Regulatory compliance backbone: WHO, EU-GMP, USFDA, UKMHRA guidelines followed in design and execution across pharmaceutical emerging markets
items.quote: Therefore, WHO, EU -GMP, USFDA, or UKMHRA. These are the backbone regulatory guidelines that are followed by the Fabtech team, be it in design or in execution.

name: Canara HSBC Life Insurance Company Ltd

items.statement: FY27 total AUM growth target ~25%
items.quote: We expect another year of approximately 25% growth in total AUM.

items.statement: FY27 consolidated profit growth target ~50%
items.quote: We expect consol profits to also grow at approximately 50%.

items.statement: FY27 exit RoAUM target ~2.5%
items.quote: We expect to exit FY27 with a return on AUM of approximately 2.5% versus the 2.1% we reported in Q4 FY26.

items.statement: Legacy book to become irrelevant by H2 FY27
items.quote: If we are talking about Legacy book next year at this time, we would be very, very surprised. It will become irrelevant by the latter half of this year, by Q4 of this year, it should become kind of so small to be irrelevant.

items.statement: Total AUM grew 25% YoY to INR1,01,230 crores in FY26
items.quote: On a consol basis, AUM was up 25% year-on-year and we ended the year at INR1,01,230 crores.

items.statement: Growth AUM grew 33% YoY to INR98,423 crores in Q4 FY26
items.quote: Growth AUM was collectively thus up 33% year-on-year to INR98,423 crores.

items.statement: Retail AUM grew 33% YoY to INR85,885 crores in FY26
items.quote: In FY26, it grew 33% year-on-year to INR85,885 crores.

items.statement: Wholesale 2.0 AUM grew 38% YoY to INR12,538 crores in Q4 FY26
items.quote: As at March 2026, the Wholesale 2.0 book stood at INR12,538 crores, which was a growth of about 38% year-on-year.

items.statement: Legacy book down 59% YoY to INR2,807 crores in FY26
items.quote: We have completed our AUM mix transition with the Legacy book down 59% year-on-year to INR2,807 crores versus the target of reducing it to INR3,000 crores to INR3,500 crores.

items.statement: Retail disbursements up 34% YoY to INR13,101 crores in Q4 FY26
items.quote: Disbursements in retail recovered from a moderate Q3 and were up 34% year-on-year to INR13,101 crores.

items.statement: Micro loans AUM up 42% YoY to INR1,384 crores in Q4 FY26
items.quote: Our micro loans AUM was up 42% year-on-year from a small base to INR1,384 crores.

items.statement: Customer franchise grew 22% YoY to 5.7 million in Q4 FY26
items.quote: Our retail customer franchise grew by 22% year-on-year to 5.7 million.

items.statement: Opened 108 branches in Q4 FY26; total network 701
items.quote: In this quarter, we opened 26 full -service branches, which we have now rechristened as urban branches. In addition to these, we have also opened 22 gold loan branches and added 60 rural branches, which we earlier called microfinance branches. We have now t aken our rural network to 136 branches. In all, our total branch network has crossed 700 in this quarter and stands at 701

items.statement: Plan to open 180 more gold loan branches in FY27 to reach ~200
items.quote: We expect to open 180 more gold loan branches in FY 27 to take our gold loan branch count to approximately 200.

items.statement: Consolidated NIM expanded 20 bps QoQ to 6.5% in Q4 FY26
items.quote: Our consolidated level NIM expanded 20 bps quarter-on-quarter to 6.5%.

items.statement: Growth book NIM at 7% in Q4 FY26
items.quote: You will also see on this slide that the consol e NIM has been continuing to close the gap with our growth book NIM, which is 7%.

items.statement: Cost of borrowing declined 11 bps QoQ to 8.84% in Q4 FY26
items.quote: Cost of borrowing during the quarter declined by 11 basis points on a Q-o-Q basis to 8.84%.

items.statement: AA+ rating may lower cost of borrowing by 50-80 bps over 3 years
items.quote: Domestic credit rating upgrade from AA to AA+ has the potential to lower our cost of borrowing by 50 to 80 basis points once we churn our current borrowing stack out and replace it with new borrowings.

items.statement: AA+ rating could lift steady-state ROEs by 3-4 percentage points
items.quote: All of this could lift steady-state ROEs by 3% to 4% percentage points.

items.statement: Retail opex to AUM fell 21 bps QoQ to 3.6% in Q4 FY26
items.quote: On opex, retail opex to AUM further came down by 21 basis points quarter-on-quarter to 3.6% per annum in quarter 4.

items.statement: Retail opex to AUM may fall further in FY27
items.quote: While we have restarted our branch expansion, the continued productivity gains for our employees and branches have the potential to take our retail opex to AUM a little bit lower than current levels over FY27.

items.statement: Retail 90+ DPD down 20 bps QoQ to 0.6% in Q4 FY26
items.quote: The stability and predictability are also visible in our credit risk outcomes, with retail 90 plus delinquencies down 20 basis points quarter-on-quarter to 0.6%.

items.statement: Growth business credit cost down marginally QoQ to 1.5% in Q4 FY26
items.quote: Growth business credit cost was also down marginally quarter-on-quarter to 1.5%.

items.statement: Consolidated GNPA and NNPA down 30 bps QoQ to 2.3% and 1.6% in Q4 FY26
items.quote: Our total GNPA and NNPA were down 30 bps quarter-on-quarter each to 2.3% and 1.6%, respectively.

items.statement: Wholesale 2.0 asset quality robust with zero NPAs
items.quote: Asset quality remained robust with zero NPAs in this book as Anand mentioned earlier.

items.statement: Micro loan portfolio almost completely normalized
items.quote: The micro loan portfolio has almost completely normalized, as you see in our 90 DPD chart that we share every quarter.

items.statement: Used car portfolio risk fell steeply in Q4 after three elevated quarters
items.quote: In our semi-secured business, which is used cars, after three quarters of elevated risk metrics, we saw a steep fall in Q4.

items.statement: Smaller ticket MSME mortgages stabilized and performing better
items.quote: Over this last quarter, however, we have seen this segment stabilize and perform noticeably better than before.

items.statement: Monitoring Middle East conflict impact on vulnerable sectors; bounce rates in April same as March
items.quote: Bounce rates in these vulnerable sectors in April have come in at the same levels as March.

items.statement: Tightened fresh underwriting in sectors sensitive to Iran conflict
items.quote: We have thus tightened fresh underwriting in these sensitive sectors.

items.statement: Average quarterly LCR 450% in Q4 FY26; cash and equivalents INR8,640 crores (8% of assets)
items.quote: Our average quarterly LCR in Q4 was 450%. We have cash and cash equivalents of INR8,640 crores, equivalent to 8% of all our assets.

items.statement: Incremental long-term borrowing cost 8.4%; short-term ~7.25%
items.quote: Our incremental borrowing cost for long-term money was 8.4%. We didn't raise much short-term at all, so I don't know, my guess would be that short-term will be like 7.25% right now if we went to the market and started raising short money.

items.statement: Received $148 million deferred proceeds from Piramal Imaging sale in Q4 FY26
items.quote: In Q4, we received deferred consideration proceeds of $148 million towards the sale of Piramal Imaging.

items.statement: Concluded Shriram Life Insurance stake sale worth INR600 crores
items.quote: We also concluded the stake sale of Shriram Life Insurance worth INR600 crores.

items.statement: Leverage (AUM/equity) increased to 3.6x in Q4 FY26 from 3x YoY; target 4.5-5x
items.quote: Leverage, which is AUM to equity, also continued to increase and we are now up at 3.6x in Q4 compared to 3x same quarter last year. We continue to progress towards our goal of 4.5 to 5x.

items.statement: Capital adequacy 19.8% as of March 2026
items.quote: Our capital adequacy is very strong at 19.8% as on March 2026.

items.statement: Accumulated tax losses INR24,600 crores; ~INR16,000 crores future profits tax-protected
items.quote: We also added INR10,110 crores to our assessed tax losses, totaling total assessed tax losses to INR24,600 crores.

items.statement: Interested in M&A in microfinance, gold loans, MSME at value pricing; nothing imminent
items.quote: We remain interested in the spaces of microfinance, gold loans, MSME, any of these spaces, you know, we remain interested and we do look at a lot of deals, but nothing's imminent.

items.statement: Operations productivity doubled in 2 years while headcount flat; AUM doubled
items.quote: You can see on this slide that operations productivity has doubled in the last 2 years. Our AUM has doubled in this period, whereas our operations staff and headcount has remained roughly flat.
